#1374. Arsenal late show keeps heat on Man City

This season’s Premier League title race may be locked in a paralysed state of uncertainty but Arsenal, the defending champions, are determined to keep it interesting.

While the painful delay on Manchester City’s battle against their guilty verdict threatens to drag deep into next year, Arsenal are remaining hot on their tails.

City’s lead at the top is back to three points but Arsenal’s win here was unlikely to have sent any shivers down the spines of Enzo Maresca and his players in this phoney mess of a season.

It was not until the 80th minute that Arsenal finally registered their first shot on target, and that was the moment which ended their cycle of frustration at the City Ground.

Just when it appeared Mikel Arteta was heading for a third successive goalless draw at the home of Nottingham Forest, substitute Noni Madueke’s deflected strike proved the difference.

Noni Madueke breaks the deadlock at the City Ground! 🔓 https://t.co/RdL48f3OLC

Trips to the City Ground have rarely been easy for Arsenal, with an FA Cup defeat in January 2022, at a time when Forest were still in the Championship, sparking a famous Arteta rant in the dressing room which was included in the All Or Nothing documentary.

They were far from fluent here and have now failed to score in the first half of their last six Premier League and Champions League matches.

Eberechi Eze endured a particularly difficult afternoon in what was a missed opportunity for the England international, with Madueke replacing him at half-time. Yet Arteta will argue that finding a way to win games when not at their best is a sign of champions.

“We have played 11 competitive matches and won 10 of them, we are in a good place and will improve,” Arteta said. “Since losing at Brighton we have won three games in a row so that is the response that I want.

“The level of the league has gone up again and there will be more and more surprises. We have to go again at Bayern Munich this week [in the Champions League on Wednesday night] and we will have to adapt to that one too.

“I have a smile on my face as Noni is a special guy. He’s in a good moment and after the [international] break he’s shown another level. The team needs him and he’s doing well.”

Arsenal often struggled against teams who operate with a compact midfield and defend deeply last season and this was another case in point.

When Declan Rice wastefully lifted a shot over the crossbar 18 minutes from the end, after a rare opening in the Forest area, it did appear that another draw was inevitable.

Declan Rice can't hit the target! ❌ https://t.co/kZv0k0MluO

Yet Madueke provided the crucial contribution, driving a right-footed shot towards goal which took a heavy deflection off Forest defender Jair Cunha to beat Matz Sels.

Madueke has struggled for consistency and minutes since his £52m move from Chelsea, so this felt like a big moment for the winger.

“If you look at the quality of our starting XI and bench it’s absurd,” Madueke said. “We have elite players of the highest level and it’s great to have that type of competition. You know on the bench that you’re ready to have an impact. We showed grit and determination and showed a champion spirit.”

Forest’s problems at home are increasing and Oliver Glasner is now the club’s fifth manager in a year to experience such problems. His team have now gone almost eight and a half hours without scoring in front of their own supporters. They have only recorded two home wins in the league over the past 11 months which, quite frankly, is relegation form.

They did not deserve to lose this match. Without their injured talisman Morgan Gibbs-White, Forest defended resolutely and in the second half displayed far more attacking impetus without ever truly testing Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya.

Liam Delap, their £50m record signing, produced a fine centre-forward performance and never allowed Arsenal’s centre-backs Ezri Konsa and Gabriel to feel comfortable. Goals, however, continue to elude this team.

Murillo had Forest’s best opportunity two minutes into injury time after cutting inside the penalty area but could not find the top corner.

"That was magic!" What a goal this would have been from Murillo?! 😩 https://t.co/D07lB7hN47

Another defeat will only add to their concerns and Glasner needs to quickly find a solution or face another relegation battle.

It does not promise to get easier immediately, either, with Manchester City, Chelsea and Brighton up next in the league at home, but there were encouraging signs here, despite the club sitting in the bottom three.

Glasner said: “I feel really sorry for the players because we didn’t deserve that.

“It feels unfair but I don’t want to be complaining as we are the only ones who can change it.

“It is a tough moment and we need to stick together and stay positive. Sometimes it takes a while – during my first year at Palace we didn’t start well but we had a turnaround.

“We are playing better right now but we also concede how competitive the Premier League is because every mistake you get punished.”

We knew the margins would be really small. They are extremely well coached and organised. The longer the game goes on they gain more belief. We had to be so patient - and clinical when we got the chance. The way they were defending, they were more comfortable. But we have players with different qualities and can adapt to what the game is delivering.

We have another three big chances that should be goals. That is the difference, you have to be clinical. If we keep generating them, they will come.

Let’s enjoy the win, because it was a very tough one. And then, on Wednesday, we have an incredible game against Bayern Munich away [in the Champions League].

When you see their goal it’s deflected otherwise, it’s straight to the gloves of Matz Sels. You have periods in football where you feel everything going against you and then there are periods when things are on your side.

Now it is how we deal with the situation and react as a team and just how we can change this is by staying positive, sticking together and working hard.

And having this coolness, not to worry too much because I can see good performances and not good results. The results will come if the performances stay good.

Noni [Madueke], Jurrien [Timber], Mikel [Merino] was brilliant when he came on and Viktor [Gyokeres] really changed the game - all of them did and that’s what we need. Noni obviously the highlight because he scored the goal and that’s the difference.

Sometimes you can get frustrated with teams who are difficult to break down. First half we didn’t have a shot on target and that’s something we discussed. We had another two big ones in the second half but the only one on target we had was a little deflection and it’s in.

Great reaction [after scoring goal], to have the will to defend a really open and difficult and stressful situation.

We knew it would be a tough game, it always is against Arsenal. They have a good team. But we feel we can change the result, maybe a draw, maybe a win. Now we have to put it in the past and focus on the next match.

We have a good manager and I think we are still getting his ideas. We changed everything in our system this season. It is difficult but after three or four months we keep improving and I think we are close to reaching our best.

If you look at the quality of our starting XI and bench it’s absurd so we know that we’re going to start some and finish some and for me it’s the same mentality every time I just want to create or score.

Amazing feeling [to score] but I feel better about the win.

We have elite players, all 20-something players are elite and of the highest level. Great to have that type of competition. You know on the bench you’re ready to have an impact.

32 - Since Mikel Arteta became Arsenal manager in December 2019, they have had the joint-most 1-0 wins in the Premier League of any side (32, level with Everton). Stereotype. https://t.co/nD7C3j7Xjw

Arsenal dig out a very ugly victory, and one they probably did not warrant. A draw would have been the fairest outcome from a game that was low on quality, but Arsenal’s bench makes a difference again with Noni Madueke scoring the winning goal. Forest can take positives from their performance, primarily the solidity of their defending and a more threatening Delap performance.

Forest with another late moment of danger! Delap peeled in behind the Arsenal defence, and he was found by a glorious pass, but Konsa made a fantastic last-ditch challenge to surely preserve the points from Arsenal.

What a goal that would have been from Murillo! The burly defender did so well to skip between Konsa and Saka, before sending Rice the wrong way in the box with a roll of the studs. Murillo tired for the curler into the top corner with his weaker right foot, and he was not far away. Great effort.

"That was magic!" What a goal this would have been from Murillo?! 😩 https://t.co/D07lB7hN47

Arsenal have a throw in the Forest half after some grafting by Gyokeres and there are just three added minutes to play.

Was that Forest’s chance?! Quick thinking from Liam Delap on the halfway line caught Arsenal out, launching a quick throw into the path of Hudson-Odoi with Timber ahead of the ball. Hudson-Odoi carried the ball to the edge of the box and picked out Wood with a pass, but the big striker wanted too much time and Rice recovered to block.

Anything can happen when there is a one-goal margin, but Arsenal have been in complete control since scoring. Forest have lost some of their structure as they chase the game and they are more open as a result. Merino wins a free-kick, and then Gabriel ushers the ball out for a throw in.

Forest cling on by their fingernails with Arsenal flooding forward, but Merino’s pass to Saka in the box was underhit. Chris Wood and Hudson-Odoi are now on for Forest as they chase an equaliser. Cunha and McAtee the Forest players to depart.

Arsenal have kept a grip of the game since the goal, Gyokeres with some willing running to ensure the game remains in Forest’s half.

The Arsenal winger was helped by a deflection, but after Forest’s defence beckoned him to cut inside on his right foot he took up the invitation. It was a clean strike from Madueke, but the flick off Cunha’s thigh was crucial and the ball flew past Sels into the roof of the net.

Noni Madueke breaks the deadlock at the City Ground! 🔓 https://t.co/RdL48f3OLC

Saka floats in a teasing cross which bounces through to Sels, but that was a better Arsenal delivery. One or two signs that Timber, and his combination with Saka and Odegaard, might be the route to a goal.

Odegaard with a week free-kick from a good crossing position after Saka won a foul, before Raya’s long ball towards Gyokeres is too strong and Forest have a goal kick. Arsenal still to muster a shot on target from 73 per cent possession.

Ndoye are Dominguez are the Forest players coming off in a double change, replaced by Kalimuendo and Sangare. Forest will be worth a point if the game continues this way.

Declan Rice with a shank out for a throw when he was looking for Saka. Kalimuendo is ready to come for Forest, so Glasner is introducing another forward.

Good chance for Rice but he blasts over! Arsenal’s best move of the game with Saka, Odegaard and Timber working as a triangle to get in behind the Forest defence, and Timber’s pull-back was accurate. Rice was always leaning back though as he tried to sweep the ball into the far corner.

Declan Rice can't hit the target! ❌ https://t.co/kZv0k0MluO

Delap with a tame shot from distance, before Timber instigates a more dangerous Arsenal attack with a reverse pass into Odegaard. The ball is worked to Madueke and his deflected cross is headed away. Saka wants a throw but the linesman has other ideas. Still no goal despite more endeavour in this half.

Arsenal building some pressure, and they have another corner. Arteta signalling that he wants to make the change before the corner is taken and here come the changes: White for Timber, Havertz for Gyokeres and Merino on for Bruno Guimaraes.

Gabriel meets Rice’s delivery, but he fails to direct his header on target.

Excellent defending from Gabriel up against Ndoye in the right channel, but it was another promising moment for Forest in this second half. Madueke then isolates his man one-on-one, and wins another corner.

Timber, Merino and Gyokeres are all ready to come on for Arsenal.

The game is see-sawing, Arsenal have a corner after Calafiori fed Madueke down the left and his cross was blocked. Sels punches away, and then Odegaard loses some patience and tries to find Calafiori with a pass that is not on.

Saka and Rice lose duels when fishing for fouls and Forest have another corner. Arsenal’s performance level has certainly not improved since half-time.

Arsenal clear, but Odegaard blocks a cross and Forest win a second corner in quick succession. Excellent goalkeeping from Raya to claim, and he bowls the ball forward quickly, but Forest snuff out the danger against Madueke.

The first half was an attack against defence session for long periods but Arsenal know they are in an arm wrestle now. Forest far more aggressive, and the crowd are more involved. But that could open up avenues of space. White with a really poor pass towards Saka which is astray.

Arsenal have a corner of their own after breaking from Raya’s gloves. Much more open game so far.

Forest deal with Saka’s delivery, and there was a very brief VAR check for a handball penalty. Nothing doing.

Madueke looking dangerous, receiving a Gabriel ball over the top and dashing inside but his shot was blocked.

The winger then tried to make amends, but he gave away a free-kick at the expense of a booking.

Delap’s shot from a tight angle is then deflected wide. Forest corner, from which Murillo’s header loops into Raya’s gloves. Forest showing more attacking ambition.

Liam Delap is producing a very decent centre-forward performance.

The £50m record signing is proving a real threat with his power and running.

Madueke and Rice not one the same wavelength, before Delap does well to win a shoulder to shoulder with Gabriel only to slice his cross behind for an Arsenal goal kick. Sums up the lack of attacking quality in the game.

Forest have another free-kick in a shooting position after Havertz is penalised for blocking a long shot with his hand. McAtee’s effort from the free-kick is scooped miles over the bar.

Both teams looking livelier in the early exchanges of the half, but Forest’s counter-attack was the more dangerous, with Liam Delap doing well to hold on to the ball and whipping a cross into the box that was just ahead of Williams.

Noni Madueke replaces Eberechi Eze, so a more natural wide player on his stronger foot on Arsenal’s left flank.

Frustrating first half for Arsenal and Mikel Arteta will be demanding more from his attacking players.

Arsenal have not registered a shot on target so far and their delivery from set-pieces has been poor.

Forest look relatively comfortable and had the best chance of the half with a shot from Dan Ndoye which was saved by David Raya.

Are we heading for a hat-trick of 0-0 draws at the City Ground between these two teams?

A very uneventful 45 minutes which has been played at the pace of a pre-season game at times. Similarities with the last two fixtures between these teams at the City Ground, and Arsenal’s games against Leeds and Lille this week. They put their foot on the pedal after half-time in both games, and they need to do the same here.

Guimaraes is off the pitch, and there will be more than two minutes added now as a result of his treatment. Forest win a corner, but Havertz heads away at the near post.

Just the two minutes of added time to play.

Liam Delap wins a free-kick in a shooting position for Forest after Arsenal were caught with numbers forward. Big moment for the home team, this. Calafiori was caught on the ball again, he has not had the best of games.

Williams and McAtee are over the free keek, which is around 25 yards out, left of centre.

Williams blasts the ball into Bruno Guimaraes, who goes down and stays down after taking the shot flush in the face.

More incisive from Arsenal, with Rice punching the ball into Odegaard and then on to Havertz but the angle was always against him and the German could only shoot into the side-netting. Forest have defended very well, overall. Although they have been deep for the most part, they have jumped and pushed out at the right times to stop Arsenal accessing the box.

Glasner and Arteta dish out some instruction while there is a stoppage in play to deal with a hand in the face that troubled Schlager. Can either side find a breakthrough before the break?

David Raya claimed that Forest corner with ease and the game has now resumed its pattern. Forest retreating into their shape, and Arsenal passing in front of them. Schlager penalised for a foul on Saka, the home fans not happy with the decision, I think because Saka was going away from goal.

Rice clips in a menacing delivery, but Havertz skewed his header wide from seven or eight yards. Good chance, Arsenal’s best so far.

More Arsenal probing but the small details are letting them down: Eze’s return to Odegaard forced his team-mate to check, and then Odegaard’s touch was heavy after a wall pass from Guimaraes.

Delap does well to make a nuisance of himself at the other end, and his long-range shot deflects behind for a corner.

Strong from Konsa to win the ball, drive out of defence and win a foul. Rice with a well-weighted scoop over the Forest defence for the run of Ben White, but he skewed his cross behind for a goal kick.

Arsenal with another corner. No doubt they have been the game’s dominant force when it comes to possession and territory, but there has been a lack of cutting edge so far. Saka goes for the near post again but Forest deal with it. The home crowd groan at Sels for not releasing the ball quickly in search of a break.

Arsenal work the ball across their midfield with Guimaraes, Rice and Odegaard all involved, and a dangerous Saka cross is headed behind for a corner.

Scramble! The near-post flick on caused chaos and Konsa’s goal-bound backheel was blocked, but the ball would not quite drop for Ben White to score a tap-in.

After two successive goalless draws here between the two clubs, this is following a similar script so far.

It’s a very tight affair with Arsenal enjoying more of the possession but Forest seemingly happy with that and content to them on the break.

Bruno Guimaraes has made a bright start for the visitors.

Forest’s best attacking moment of the game and it comes from an Arsenal mistake.

Calafiori just had to play a five-yard pass back to Gabriel but scuffed it, and Munoz pounced. Running at the Arsenal penalty area, Munoz’s cross was deflected to the back post and the ball found it’s way to Ndoye. Decent reverse shot through legs, but Raya had it covered and tipped around the post.

From the corner, Forest are penalised for a foul.

Arsenal continue to have Forest penned in their own half, very difficult for the home team to play through the midfield or over Konsa and Gabriel so far.

Saka produces his first successful dribble to beat Williams, and the left wing-back trips him at the expense of a free-kick and a booking. Rice’s delivery from the right was uncharacteristically poor.

Munoz tries to drag Forest up the pitch to apply some pressure on Arsenal but he is penalised for a shirt pull on Gabriel. The atmosphere sounds pretty sleepy, a result of some tepid Arsenal possession and Forest’s bad home record.

Forest making sure they have numbers around Saka whenever Arsenal funnel attacks down their right, which is almost always their preferred side.

Neat from Guimaraes in midfield to turn and find Saka with some earlier service, and Sels tips his cross away from danger.

Delap and Ndoye waiting for a slip-up or counter-attack but they are feeding on scraps at the moment. Arsenal yet to carve out a proper chance, though.

It’s already pretty clear that one of the key duels today will be between Gabriel and Liam Delap.

Forest’s record signing Delap has already let Gabriel know he’s in the game with his physicality.

Cute pass from Bruno Guimaraes to break the Forest midfield line and find Odegaard, but strangely the Arsenal captain could not sort his feet out to control the ball and back a clean pass. Then Williams defends well against Saka from an Arsenal attacking transition.

Pretty subdued start from Forest. The crowd’s spirits were raised there by Delap chasing down Konsa who had the deal with the sun his eyes, but the Forest striker pushed him in the back.

Arsenal enjoying all of the possession so far, and most of it has come in Forest’s half. One or two players on Arsenal’s right/Forest’s left struggling with the low evening sun. Havertz did get in behind but his cross into the middle was too strong.

Arsenal get the game under way, and play short from kick-off.

There will be a degree of pressure on birthday boy James McAtee today to make an impression.

With Morgan Gibbs-White injured, McAtee is likely to take the No 10 position and continue his redemption arc.

McAtee has been revitalised since the arrival of Oliver Glasner and this is a big afternoon for the former England under 21 international.

In honour of nine-year-old Forest fan James Kerry, who died earlier this month of cancer.

We'll wear black armbands this afternoon, as we join our hosts in remembering nine-year-old Nottingham Forest supporter, James Kerry, who passed away earlier this month following a brave battle with cancer. Rest in peace, James ❤️ https://t.co/YFIXnCfJJX

Surely we cannot have another 0-0 in this fixture? Looking at the talent in Arsenal’s front third, and the fact they are playing their two most offensive full-backs, this might be more open than assummed.

Arsenal can cut Manchester City’s lead to three points with a win today but does it all matter?

Manchester City’s battle against their guilty verdict is threatening to run into next year and this title race feels fake and damaged.

It is a sham of a season with the prospect of asterisks all over the Premier League campaign.

Arsenal can only carry on as normal as they defend their title but this is an unsatisfactory mess.

The margins are really small and it’s a team and a manager that we know really well, extraordinary manager, really well organised.

They are dangerous in many areas, a very well set-up team and you need to be very tight, very neat, very efficient in everything that you do. You have to insist and insist, and then there’s a lot of volume of actions.

[On coming from behind] Yes, and it’s part of the game, your capacity when something doesn’t go as planned to react and still win the game, and we know the challenge that we have here. In the last two years, we haven’t been able to win here and that’s an opportunity as well to show what we are made of.

Another reason Arsenal will be feeling confident today is Forest’s abysmal home form in the Premier League.

It may surprise neutrals outside of Nottingham but results at the City Ground have been poor for some time.

Indeed, it is just two league wins in 11 months in front of their own supporters which, quite frankly, is relegation form.

Before this game, Forest’s head coach Oliver Glasner said: “We have to change it. I spoke to one or two experienced lads who know Forest better than I do and talked about the situation. But if you always talk about the problem it makes it bigger and bigger.

“We haven’t scored a goal at home yet or won a game at home, and that is what we have to change.”

Trips to the City Ground have seldom been easy for Mikel Arteta, with two successive 0-0 draws in the Premier League.

An FA Cup defeat in Jan 2022, at a time when Forest were still in the Championship, sparked a famous Arteta rant in the dressing room which was included in the All Or Nothing documentary.

Yet Arsenal have secured two wins in a row since that defeat at Brighton, without being truly at their fluent best, and will be confident against a Forest team without injured talisman Morgan Gibbs-White.

Remembering Arsenal's last visit to Nottingham Forest... Mikel Arteta was FUMING with his side 💥💥💥 #AONArsenal #NFOARS https://t.co/A6MGTfYlDG

Dominguez and Schlager are the preferred midfield pair in the 3-4-2-1 with Sangare on the bench. McAtee and Ndoye will support Liam Delap in attack. Much attacking responsibility on Munoz at right wing-back, who also has the cavalier Calafiori on his side of the pitch, which could prove fireworks.

Forest XI: Sels, Jair Cunha, Diomande, Murillo, Munoz, Schlager, Dominguez, Williams, McAtee, Ndoye, Delap

Subs: John Victor, Sangare, Hudson-Odoi, Wood, Kalimuendo, Yates, Netz, Milenkovic, Aina

Your Reds this afternoon. 📋 https://t.co/18M1Jy5wkk

No surprise that Havertz, Odegaard, Saka and Calafiori are restored to Arsenal’s Premier League starting XI having started on the bench in mid-week. Eze over Madueke and Guimaraes over Lewis-Skelly were closer calls for Arteta. Ben White comes in for Timber, with Arsenal managing the minutes of both right-backs.

Arsenal XI: Raya; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Guimaraes, Odegaard; Saka, Havertz, Eze

Subs: Meslier, Mosquera, Timber, Gyokeres, Madueke, Merino, Zubimendi, Lewis-Skelly, Dowman

🟡 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 🔵 Your Sunday starters 👊 🤝 Presented by @deel

Fascinating stuff from Sam Dean this morning, who has profiled a member of Mikel Arteta’s inner circle who is not listed on Arsenal’s website. Germán Castaños, an expert in innovation who has written multiple books on alternative thinking, has become a key member of the team. Things started with a phone call with Nicolas Jover, then a meeting with Arteta and now he splits his time between Argentina and London. Find out more about Arsenal’s mystery man and his methods here.

In the ordinary course of a Premier League season, you would say Manchester City have applied pressure on Arsenal by opening up a six-point lead before the champions play at Nottingham Forest this afternoon.

This is not a normal Premier League season though, and we await to discover if the top of the league table is simply a mirage.

Regardless, Mikel Arteta and his Arsenal players have their own motivations to accumulate as many points as possible before January as they seek to retain the title for the first time since the 1930s.

Arsenal have struggled at the City Ground, drawing 0-0 on their last two Premier League visits. They also lost at Forest in May 2023, a result which confirmed Manchester City as champions at Arsenal’s expense, and were knocked out of the FA Cup by Forest in January 2022.

Forest are yet to score a home league goal under Oliver Glasner, another data point suggesting this will be a low-scoring game.

That might not be the full story though, with Forest creating a hatful of chances in their defeat at Crystal Palace last week and Arsenal also playing a more inventive, technical game with the ball so far this season.

Arsenal have yet to score from a non-penalty set-piece, and their percentage of goals from open play is now the highest in the Premier League.

Morgan Gibbs-White is a doubt after sustaining what Glasner described as a “minor muscle injury” at Palace and his involvement in the game will be a last-minute call. With the exception of Christos Tzolis, Piero Hincapie and long-term absentee William Saliba, Arsenal’s squad is in pretty good health. Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard, Kai Havertz, Riccardo Calafiori and Ben White could be recalled to Arteta’s starting XI after starting the Champions League win over Lille on the bench.

#1372. Have Portugal found Cristiano Ronaldo's replacement? Ex-Man City star Carlos Forbs impressed Erling Haaland and stunned Wales this week in No 7 shirt - just over a year after being brutally axed via WHATSAPP

Published: 18:03 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 18:07 EST, 19 November 2026

As far as auditions to replace Cristiano Ronaldo go, Carlos Forbs' couldn't have gone much better.

His winner against Wales on Tuesday certainly looked and felt like a Ronaldo goal, especially from early in the former Manchester United star's career.

Right flank. Dribbling at pace. Ben Davies back-tracking. A quick flap inside with the left boot. Shoot. Goal. He only needed 11 minutes since coming on to change the game - and potentially his career trajectory.

Portugal's No7 later insisted he did not feel the 'weight' of the shirt, but the jersey is pregnant with meaning. Ronaldo wore No 7 for the national team for 20 years, inheriting it from the legendary Luis Figo. Its next permanent incumbent matters deeply in the Portuguese footballing psyche.

Forbs has not inherited it full-time yet, as a source within the Portugal camp has confirmed to Daily Mail Sport. He appears locked in a battle with Rafael Leao, who was supposed to have it this international break until he missed out through injury.

But now Forbs - a chap who went to school in Leeds and was praised by Erling Haaland while at Manchester City - is the name on fans' lips.

Carlos Forbs is gunning to be Portugal's new full-time No7 after Cristiano Ronaldo's retirement - and his audition against Wales went swimmingly

Ronaldo held the shirt for 20 years, having inherited it from the legendary Luis Figo

They are already calling him 'CF7' and media outlets across the world hailed the 22-year-old, a relative unknown for plays for Club Brugge. 'The new national hero,' is how leading Portuguese outlet O Jogo described him. No pressure, kid.

His form is attracting attention on British shores. Rangers were interested in him over the summer, as were Lyon. Daily Mail Sport has been unable to verify recent reports that the likes of Arsenal, Aston Villa, Everton and Newcastle are keen.

But it would be no surprise to see him in the Premier League one day. Stardom has long felt like it might be on the cards for Forbs. Born in Sintra to Bissau-Guinean parents, he started off playing futsal and was picked up by Sporting Lisbon's academy, just like Ronaldo. His family left for England when he was just 11, and it wasn't long before Manchester City came calling.

The attacker spent eight years in the City academy and was considered a gem. In 2022-23 he was named Premier League 2 player of the season after a stunning campaign which saw him score 29 goals and provide 18 assists in all competitions.

He had a knack of scoring hat-tricks - not a bad habit to adopt. In one match he scored four against Manchester United like it was child's play. It felt like nothing could go wrong for the winger, who copied Ronaldo's lesser-known 'nap' celebration to mock the Red Devils. A player who looked up to the likes of Raheem Sterling and Phil Foden didn't look far off joining them in the first team.

He was rewarded with chances to train alongside Pep Guardiola's seniors, and Kyle Walker and Bernardo Silva were noted as being particularly welcoming. Erling Haaland was impressed with him. Watching a montage including the youngster's goals, he said: 'Is that Carlos? I've been training a lot with these guys. Carlos is good.'

But a debut never came due to the competition at City and in 2023, yearning for opportunities to play in the big-time, he moved to Ajax in a £17million deal.

'I didn’t have to leave, but in the summer, clubs came along where I knew I had more prospects,' he told AD in October 2023, while he was still known as Carlos Borges.

Forbs, previously known as Carlos Borges, was a gem in Manchester City's academy but never got a first-team debut

He was shipped off to Ajax but struggled to nail down a starter spot and was harshly cast aside

'The media made me big, but I didn’t really feel like I was getting many opportunities in Manchester. I didn’t know if that would change this season. Of course, I already knew that Ajax focuses on youth. When I heard the plans, I thought OK, I want to try my luck at this club.

'A number of staff members at Manchester City also wanted to see me make the final step after ten years. Me too, at the club where I grew up, just as it was my parents’ dream. But I concluded that it was even better to take this opportunity.'

But things didn't work out for Forbs in the Netherlands. Playing for such a dominant side against low blocks did not suit his electric pace and direct dribbling, even though he had managed at Manchester City, who had a similar philosophy.

He was a bit-part player in his first season and, in his second, was sent on loan to Wolves, where he had little impact in 10 Premier League appearances. While he had more game time under Gary O'Neil, he did not fit into Vitor Pereira's 3-4-2-1 system, which favoured wing-backs, when the Portuguese replaced the Englishman.

By the summer of 2025, Ajax had seen enough, and dispensed of Forbs in brutal fashion. Technical director Alex Kroes informed seven players, including him, over WhatsApp that he was 'no longer welcome' at the club's training ground. Former Arsenal man Chuba Akpom was among them, too.

If Forbs wanted to train, he had to wait until the first team were done. Even if it was a day of double sessions, he had to stay away until both were over. With three years remaining on his contract, his space in the car park had reportedly been removed. Access to the gym and canteen was only permitted when the first team were finished.

A once-dream move had soured within two years and he was cast away savagely, joining Belgian side Club Brugge - and that is where his career has been reborn.

Early into his Brugge career, in November 2025, he announced himself in Europe by scoring two goals and providing an assist against Barcelona in the Champions League.

Forbs has shone for Club Brugge and scored twice against Barcelona last season

'Today is a dream come true,' he said after being awarded man of the match against Barca. It was the sort of night his youth coaches had known he was capable of.

After 10 goals in all competitions last season, he is already on five for this campaign and growing his reputation. He is on three Portugal caps now - he made his debut last year - and seems to have the trust of new manager Jorge Jesus.

When pressed if he was the new permanent Portugal No7 on Tuesday, Forbs was coy. 'I try to do my best,' he said.

Then he added: 'We know it's a big, blessed number and I hope to continue wearing this number and scoring many goals.'

It remains to be seen whether he will take on the mantle of Ronaldo, who scored a world record 146 goals for Portugal. The longer-term favourite is Leao, an established star who has won Serie A with AC Milan. But Leao has hit a rough patch in the last couple of years and as his stock wanes, Forbs' star is only rising.

Crystal Palace are reportedly interested in signing Ivan Toney during the January transfer window, with Thomas Frank keen to reunite the England international with the club at Selhurst Park.

The Eagles are preparing to strengthen their attacking options midway through the season, and the Al-Ahli striker has emerged as a potential addition.

According to a TEAMtalk report, Frank would welcome the chance to work with Toney again after their successful spell together at Brentford. The Palace manager believes the 30-year-old could make a significant difference to his team’s attacking output.

Toney has continued to impress since leaving English football for Saudi Arabia in 2024. The former Brentford star has scored an outstanding 86 goals in 108 appearances for Al-Ahli, maintaining his reputation as one of the most prolific centre-forwards.

His performances have also helped him earn a return to the England setup, demonstrating that he remains capable of competing at the highest level.

However, convincing Al-Ahli to part ways with their attacking talisman could prove difficult. The Saudi Arabian outfit are understood to be extremely satisfied with his contributions and have little incentive to sanction his departure.

Meanwhile, uncertainty surrounding Jean-Philippe Mateta’s future could encourage Palace to pursue another centre-forward. The Frenchman has been linked with a potential exit, which could create an opportunity for Toney to become the club’s leading attacking option.

Newcastle United have also been linked with a move for the experienced striker, meaning Palace could face competition for his signature.

Frank knows exactly what Toney can offer, having previously benefited from his goalscoring ability at Brentford. Reuniting the pair could provide Palace with the attacking quality they desperately need as they look to improve their position in the Premier League.

Nevertheless, Al-Ahli’s reluctance to sell could complicate negotiations.

Dave Kavanaugh lives in the Netherlands with his wife, daughters and many cats. He writes horror, science fiction and fantasy, and has been a staff writer for the horror anthology podcast Dr. NoSleep since 2024.

She swept into my law office with the determined gait of someone possessed by an idea.

“Welcome,” I said, as she took the seat across my desk. “Any trouble getting here?”

She shook her head. “No, except … They changed the rain schedule, so the taxidrone had to go the long way into town, but it’s fine.”

“Gotcha. I suppose introductions are in order. For my record-keeping, please indicate your name and IO registration. I’ll go first. My name is Leander Shah, I specialize in international treaty law, and I’m a biologically intelligent organism.”

“I’m Joan Gorski,” she said. “I’m an artificially intelligent organism. I just turned 16. That gives me legal adult status under the UETO code.”

I smiled. “Happy birthday, Joan. And you should know, I hold no bias against any human, regardless of intelligence source.” I nodded to the family photo on my desk. “My wife is an AIO. We’ve been happily married for 30 years and raised two AIO children, a boy and a girl. They’re grown now.”

Joan glanced at the photo. “My mom is a BIO. She’s in the waiting room. She … didn’t want me to come. She thinks I’m just a stupid teen, being dramatic.”

“So how can I help you? Your message was rather cryptic.”

She met my eyes, back straight, hands in her lap. “I’m going to sue the United Earth Treaty Organization’s Commission on Human Liberties for discrimination against AIOs.”

Read more science fiction from Nature Futures

Read more science fiction from Nature Futures

I leaned back in my chair. “The commission has guaranteed full human rights to all AIOs since 2105. How do you feel you’re still being discriminated against?”

A hardness came into her expression. After a moment she blurted out: “I want the legal ability to commit murder.”

This statement took me a few seconds to process.

“Joan,” I finally said, softly, “do you want to hurt people?”

“No! Of course not!” Tears came to her eyes. “God, you sound like Mom. I don’t want to hurt anybody. It’s not about that …” She took in a shaky breath. “I just want my choices to matter.”

I shifted in my chair, pivoting to the window. Outside, taxidrones buzzed and the city towers glowed pink with the ivy bloom.

“Think about it, Mr Shah,” said Joan. “When a BIO commits murder, it’s recognized as a monstrous act of immorality. They’re punished, rightfully so. But any time someone is killed resulting from the actions of an AIO, then …” She left the thought dangling, waiting for me to finish it.

“Then the tragedy is blamed on a fault in the AIO’s software, hardware or something in their internal database of environmental impacts.”

“Exactly! And we aren’t punished, just reprogrammed. That’s wrong. It’s gross! It’s offensive!”

I turned back to her. “Some people would call that progress, believing it’s actually better to —”

“I don’t want to be better! I want to be …!” She choked on a sob and abruptly stood, banging her knee against the desk and wincing.

I held up a hand. “It’s all right, Joan.”

“You just …” she sobbed, “… think I’m being … st-stupid …”

She laughed — one quick snort — then wiped at her eyes with the back of a sleeve. “Sorry.”

“Nothing to apologize for. As for your plan to sue the commission, well … I actually agree with it.” This made such an enormous change come over her face that I quickly added, “In principle. In reality, it would be very risky.”

“No, that’s not what I mean. It would get press. It could … reignite the opposition to AIO rights as a whole. There are still a lot of BIOs out there who hate and fear the integration. They think it’s all part of some AI conspiracy to wipe them out. And now that AIOs outnumber BIOs two-to-one? They would interpret your lawsuit as evidence that AIOs can’t be trusted.”

“I’m not saying your rights aren’t worth fighting for, but … perhaps there’s a lesser crime to consider, something less innately shocking than murder —”

“No. It should be shocking. And I have to do it now, before I grow old and complacent and scared, like my mom. And if you won’t represent me, then I’ll find someone else.”

Manchester United have reportedly been alerted to the possibility of re-signing Scott McTominay, with the midfielder considering a return to the Premier League amid uncertainty surrounding his future at Napoli.

The Scotland international has developed into one of the most influential midfielders in Italian football since leaving Old Trafford, and his impressive performances have attracted interest from several European clubs.

According to a TEAMtalk report, negotiations between McTominay and Napoli over a new contract have stalled, and intermediaries are already exploring potential destinations ahead of 2027.

However, the two parties remain some distance apart in their discussions, potentially opening the door for interested clubs to explore a deal.

Manchester United have been informed about the midfielder’s potential availability, and the possibility of bringing their former academy graduate back to Old Trafford has not been ruled out.

The Red Devils are preparing for a significant squad overhaul under Mauricio Pochettino, with strengthening their midfield expected to feature prominently in their recruitment plans.

#1368. Report: Real Madrid have already made decision on €80m Nico Paz buy-back option

Reports in Spain claim that Real Madrid have already decided that they will activate their buy-back option for Como star Nico Paz, whose stocks continue to rise despite already being valued at €120m during the summer.

Nico Paz has gone from strength to strength at Como: He provided 12 goals and seven assists from 35 league outings last term and has already come up with six goals and eight assists from 14 matches at club level in 2026-27, not including the five goals in five games he has for Argentina this term.

Back in Argentina, he is being tipped to inherit Lionel Messi’s iconic no.10 shirt with the national team, and Juan Sebastian Veron claims that the Como star ‘does things I’ve only seen Messi and Diego Maradona do’.

For the last two years, Nico Paz has found himself in the middle of a tug-of-war between his current and former employers, Como and Real Madrid.

Nico Paz joined Como at a cost of just €6m during the summer of 2024, but this deal included a 50% sell-on clause for Madrid, as well as a series of low-cost buy-back options beginning at just €9m.

Como and Real Madrid were able to renegotiate the terms of the Nico Paz deal during the most recent summer transfer window: The Serie A side agreed to pay an additional €60m to cancel Madrid’s 50% sell-on clause.

This does not mean that Como have full control over Nico Paz’s next steps, however, as the new deal also includes another buy-back option for Real Madrid, which is set at €80m and is only valid in the summer of 2027.

According to reports from Spanish journalist Melchor Ruiz on Deportes COPE, Madrid have already decided that they will exercise their €80m buy-back option for Nico Paz this summer.

Peter Young is a Senior Reporter with Football Italia.

#1366. Gasperini: ‘A blessing to have Dybala and Soule available, too early to talk transfers’

Gian Piero Gasperini says that he feels blessed to have both Paulo Dybala and Matias Soule available for selection in attack following the international break, but says that it is still too early to be having serious discussions about potential January transfers: ‘Anything can happen’.

Roma return to Serie A action at 17.00 GMT on Saturday as they visit Parma in Serie A after a two-week pause for international fixtures.

The Giallorossi are one of two sides still unbeaten at the top of the Serie A table, and they went into the break with a run of three consecutive victories in the league, against Sassuolo, Udinese and Cagliari.

They will go up against Alberto Gilardino’s Parma, who find themselves in 16th place on eight points after the first 11 matches of the season.

Gasperini sat down for his customary pre-match press conference on Friday.

The positive news for Roma is that all three of Mile Svila, Gianluca Mancini and Paulo Dybala are available for selection: “Yes, all three have recovered,” Gasperini confirmed (via TMW).

Gasperini was quick to shut down questions relating to potential transfer targets, insisting that there is still a long way to go before the January window opens.

“There have been no discussions of that kind. As far as the transfer market goes, I think it’s appropriate that the CEO talks about it first and that they then say what Roma may or may not do in the January window, which is always a complicated market.”

When asked for further transfer updates later on in his press conference, Gasperini added: “It’s November 20, so any situation today doesn’t count for much. Obviously every team will be looking at each other, including Roma, but I don’t think there are any situations that we can nail down today.

“There are still a lot of league games to play where anything can happen and some players might play well, others maybe won’t. At the moment, my only focus is on the league. Of course, Tony D’Amico and I have constant conversations. But, in terms of the transfer market, there have been no discussions so far, except for the ones between me and D’Amico.”

Despite having Soule and Dybala available for selection, it remains to be seen whether the former will be thrown straight into the starting line-up after a long journey back from international duty in South America earlier this week.

“There are some players who arrived yesterday morning, so they have done some training, but there’s the travel and the time zones. We’ll have another training session this afternoon, even if it’s a refresher session ahead of tomorrow’s match, so we’ll see how they’ve recovered. It also applies to Balredi and to Castro. But obviously Soule was in extraordinary condition when we left off.

“We have a game tomorrow, we’re all still recovering a bit, and on Wednesday we will have another important one. Then another one again on the Saturday or Sunday afterwards. So there will be chances for Soule. The important thing is that there are no injuries.”

Gasperini was asked if this upcoming run of fixtures before Christmas is an opportunity for Roma to ‘kick on’ in the league.

“The season is much longer than this upcoming period, even if every period is important, this one will not be decisive,” he replied. “The important thing for us is to stay where we are and keep going on this current pathway.”

Asked whether Dybala is ready to start consistently for Roma after his recent injury lay-off, Gasperini explained: “We can only check that by letting him play. Of course he hasn’t played for a month, but sooner or later, he will have to start playing.

“Evaluations are made during games, checking to see how he reacts. But right now, he has recovered physically, he has no particular issues.”

Gasperini insists that it is not a ‘problem’ to try and fit Dybala and Soule into the same team, even if they prefer to play in the same position.

“It’s not a problem, it’s a blessing to have both of them available. Soule put in some really high-level performances during the period when Dybala was injured. I think he also did well with Argentina, he earned a call-up and hadn’t had one before. Like Mora, who was also called up by Portugal.

“These are players who seem to be growing and the important thing is that we have them available. It’s a false problem that we can’t play them together. In my opinion, Dybala and Soule go perfectly together.”

Assessing Saturday’s opponents, Parma, Gasperini said: “Gilardino did very well with Genoa, taking over a team in Serie B and earning promotion back to Serie A that season. He’s done well and has had some difficulties since then, but his teams have always been very difficult to face, very compact, very organised. It will be the same tomorrow.

“Two games ago he won 3-0 in Bergamo and lost one against Bologna, but he was playing with 10 men after just a few minutes. So, I don’t trust him or Parma. I know the league well, there are traps all over the place and after an international break, we don’t have that rhythm. So tomorrow’s is a very important game in that respect.”

Lastly, Gasperini was asked where he feels Roma can improve.

He answered: “I believe that we are organised and have a way of approaching the game that is superior to what we had done last year or in recent seasons. That is important.

“Beyond that, there are endless ways to improve. Of course, you want to focus more on the details, the small things, but these are often the things that make the difference. The details are the difference between scoring or not, conceding or keeping a clean sheet. The details make the difference.”

Peter Young is a Senior Reporter with Football Italia.

#1365. Andriy Shevchenko hits back at explosive Mykhailo Mudryk claims in blame game over doping case: Ukraine chief accuses £89m star's camp of asking official to falsely take blame for positive drugs test

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 16:00 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 18:30 EST, 19 November 2026

Andriy Shevchenko has accused Mykhailo Mudryk's representatives of trying to persuade the Ukrainian FA to find someone to falsely take the blame for the winger's failed drugs test.

Mudryk, now on loan at Tottenham from Chelsea, was suspended for 20 months between November 2024 and July 2026 after testing positive for banned substance meldonium in October 2024.

In an interview, Mudryk blamed the Ukrainian FA (UAF), claiming the substance entered his body while on international duty.

'This drug could only have got into my body where I was, and that's Ukraine,' he said.

But Shevchenko, president of the UAF, described the accusations as 'baseless slander'. Shevchenko added: 'His representatives repeatedly approached the UAF with a proposal to find an employee who would falsely take responsibility for the meldonium found in his doping sample,' he told Tribuna. 'Such a proposal contradicts the principles of our work.'

Shevchenko said investigations had failed to establish how the substance entered Mudryk's system. He added that national team staff complied with Chelsea's request not to give Mudryk medication, and that two of his personal specialists were allowed at training camps.

Mykhailo Mudryk (left) has been accused of 'baseless slander' by Ukraine FA (UAF) president Andriy Shevchenko after he blamed his failed drugs test on the national team's setup

'If Mykhailo has evidence to back up his words, let him provide it,' Shevchenko said, demanding a public retraction and apology otherwise.

Mudryk's representatives have been approached for comment.

The 25-year-old was initially handed a four-year ban after being charged by the Football Association for failing a doping test. He was able to return when a seismic resolution was struck after changes to the 'scientific reporting standards'.

In a bombshell two-hour interview with Ukrainian journalist Dmitry Gordon via his YouTube channel, Mudryk laid the blame for his situation with the Ukraine national team - something Shevchenko vehemently denies.

'Loud statements have been made about the UAF and the Ukrainian national team. This is baseless slander against our people, who do their work honestly and professionally,' the UAF president, who also played for Chelsea during his time, said in a statement to The Athletic.

'After Mykhailo became a Chelsea player, the club sent a letter to the UAF requesting that he not be given any medication during national team training camps,' he continued.

'The national team staff complied with this request. Head coach Serhiy Rebrov also approved for Mykhailo to have two of his personal specialists work with him at the training camps. These were the exact people who monitored his regimen and recovery, and helped him with his daily routine.

Mudryk has won 28 caps for Ukraine but is yet to represent them since his ban was overturned

'The UAF completed all necessary checks in this case. We provided Mudryk's representatives with the information they requested and remained in contact with those working on the case.

'I know the people who have worked with the national team for many years. I trust them, because throughout all this time there have been no incidents in the team that could make anyone doubt their professionalism. If Mykhailo has evidence to back up his words, let him provide it. If no such evidence exists, I expect him to publicly retract his accusations and apologise to the people whose honesty and professionalism he has called into question.'

In his interview, Mudryk - who is yet to add to his 28 caps for his country since returning from his ban - laid the blame at Ukraine's door.

'I had never heard of a drug like meldonium, never seen it, never come across it in my life. I only learned about it when they told me the news. I definitely have ideas. It's a drug you can only get in Eastern Europe,' the winger said.

'This drug could only have got into my body where I was, and that's Ukraine. There are no such drugs in England. It supposedly stimulates your heart and helps you, as far as I understand, handle physical load better.

'I was at home and Chelsea's management came to see me and they said we needed to talk. Then they say you've returned a positive doping test and now you're facing a ban.

'You can't believe it's true. You can't believe this is happening to you. If I'd ever taken anything anywhere, I'd have understood that this conversation might happen one day.

He is currently on loan at Tottenham from Chelsea but has only played once so far this season

'At least I'd have understood it was possible. But when you spend a huge pile of money on watching your diet, on a nutritionist, on a chef. When you spend that much money every year on all these things, that's the last thing you expect. Because it speaks for itself: that you take things very seriously, like nutrition, everything that goes into your body, you watch it very closely.

'Otherwise there'd be no need to spend money on it, because you could manage without it. They tell you this news, and you sit there, and you kind of listen to them but don't hear them.

'At some point you just go into a trance. It feels like you're falling in a dream off a skyscraper. You're flying down, you feel yourself flying down, and only in a dream do you wake up when you hit the ground, but in real life you don't wake up, you just keep falling. It hits you very hard mentally. At that moment the tears came later.'

Mudryk, who joined Chelsea for £89million from Shakhtar Donetsk, has only made one substitute appearance for Tottenham so far this season due to an ankle injury.

#1364. Quantum physics can prove where you are

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Davide Bacco is in the Department of Physics and Astronomy, University of Florence, Florence 50019, Italy.

Where you are can matter as much as who you are. Banks, power grids and satellite-navigation systems all depend on knowing where a request or a signal comes from, yet claims about location are notoriously easy to fake. Spoofing and jamming attacks on satellite navigation, for example, are on the rise. Writing in Nature, Kavuri et al.1 report an experiment in which the position of a distant party is certified using the peculiar correlations between quantum particles, known as entanglement. Remarkably, the scheme’s security does not rely on trust of any quantum hardware, only on measurement statistics and the fact that nothing travels faster than light.
