Maresca said: “I’m not worried about Marc at all, he is playing every game since the season started for us and the national team so it’s not easy. He is ok, it [taking him off] was just a technical decision and like in all games managers make changes. He was on a yellow card and sometimes one yellow card can be dangerous.”

When asked if the goals were avoidable, Maresca said: “Absolutely, both. Sometimes you have to be a bit more lucky because we only conceded those two chances. We will try again to win at Villa next season. I don’t think we deserved to lose but we learn from that and move on. You can always learn something. For sure there are things we can do better today.”

While much of the focus will be on City’s 100 per cent start to the league coming to an end, Emery got everything right here. From his team selection to his set-up and substitutions, he outsmarted Maresca on many levels. After the game, Villa defender Matty Cash described his manager as “a tactical genius”.

It was four years ago to the day that Emery grabbed this famous club by the shirt and collar and gave them an almighty shake. After a summer of much instability including many player sales, he appears to have already struck a formula with his newly assembled team.

There were a number of fine individual performances from many of the summer arrivals, such as Jackson, goalkeeper Zion Suzuki and Johan Manzambi.

Emery said: “We were very motivated and Manchester City is the best team in the world so this is the level. This year we started so poorly and we needed time to understand how we improve. The players showed the capacity to retrieve the level we’ve had over the last few years.

“Nicolas is more mature and very demanding of himself to improve. Earlier this season he was shooting over the crossbar but he is now finding the corners. There is still work to do and 11 points is not enough but we are feeling better.”

Villa were fierce from the start and ahead after six minutes. Guéhi’s mistake was punished by John McGinn, with the ball dropping to Jackson who crashed a shot into the roof of the net.

The home team did require Suzuki to produce saves to stop efforts from Iliman Ndiaye, Rayan Cherki and Abdukodir Khusanov as City responded. Ndiaye also struck the outside of the post and City were level seven minutes into the second half with Erling Haaland nodding in Ndiaye’s cross at the far post. Haaland had touched the ball just eight times in the opening 45 minutes but invariably only needs one chance.

He writes: “With Pep Guardiola and Jürgen Klopp having departed the Premier League, there can now be little doubt that Unai Emery is the best manager in England’s top division. And by some distance.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Aston Villa vs Manchester City.

Premier League leaders City will attempt to maintain their flawless start to the season when they visit Villa Park for Saturday’s lunchtime kick-off.

The match marks the first meeting between the sides since the final weekend of last season, when Villa secured a 2-1 victory at the Etihad in Pep Guardiola’s final game in charge at City.

Enzo Maresca became the first manager in City’s Premier League history to win his opening seven fixtures, lifting his side three points clear of title holders Arsenal. Only Chelsea in 2005-06 and Liverpool in 2019-20 have managed a longer winning start to a top-flight campaign. Following a 3-2 victory against Ipswich Town last weekend, City rebounded from a European setback against Paris Saint-Germain by delivering a commanding 5-1 Champions League win over AEK Athens on Wednesday.

However, Unai Emery’s side will present a formidable challenge. Aston Villa enter the contest on a seven-match unbeaten streak across all competitions, headlined by a perfect record in the Champions League following midweek success against Viking FK.

Villa’s domestic form has also improved, taking seven points from their last three league outings, including a 1-0 away victory at Newcastle United in Emery’s 100th Premier League match as manager. Sitting 12th in the table, Villa remain on the hunt for their first home league win of the season, though their impressive European performances at Villa Park provide significant momentum.

Emery’s men completed a league double over City last term, including a 1-0 win on home turf. Should Villa claim victory again on Saturday, it would mark the first time in the Premier League era that they have recorded three consecutive victories over the Manchester club.

Of course, City’s campaign remains overshadowed by the recent guilty verdict from the Premier League over financial regulations.

#1323. 12 Footballers to Miss Most Penalties Since 2001

Scoring from 12 yards isn’t as easy as it looks with some of the best football players in the history of the sport guilty of missing many penalties. Despite this, there are some very good penalty takers in the modern game who are able to block out the noise and pick their spot.

Typically, every team has a designated spot-kick taker and this player will be able to thrive under pressure and have an accurate ball-striking technique. However, even the most consistent penalty-kick takers can be prone to the occasional error, with goalkeepers such as Emi Martinez being known for his ability to save penalties.

On this list of the players with the most penalties missed, there are some surprising inclusions, such as spot-kick expert Cristiano Ronaldo, who ranks highly. With that in mind, here are the 12 players who have missed the most penalties in the 21st century.

Misses in penalty shootouts have not been counted in the individual tallies. And if two players are level on the number of penalty misses, then the player who has the worst conversion rate will rank higher.

The Argentine had a 77.4% conversion rate from penalties, which is far from being considered poor. However, this number is inflated due to the sheer number of penalties that the striker took. He scored 48 during his illustrious career and missed 14.

Aguero will be remembered for his pathetic penalty attempt in his final appearance for Manchester City. The talented forward tried an audacious panenka, which was caught with ease by Chelsea goalkeeper Edouard Mendy. This was a costly miss too, as in the second half Chelsea came from behind to win the Premier League encounter 2-1 in the dying moments.

Veteran Antonio Di Natale had a wonderful career and will be remembered more for his impressive performances in Serie A rather than his penalty misses. He won the Serie A top goalscorer award in 2010 and he also won the Serie A Italian Footballer of the Year award in the same year.

One year later he reclaimed the top goalscorer award after another brilliant league campaign. The lethal finisher retired in 2016 as Udinese’s all-time top scorer with 227 goals to his name. Out of the 44 spot-kicks Di Natale took, he missed just 14, giving him a 75.8% conversion rate.

Harry Kane is in the conversation when you think of the greatest penalty takers of all time. The Englishman is usually ice-cold from 12 yards, often smashing the ball into the corners with power and pinpoint accuracy. He has a mightily impressive 87.5% conversion rate, the highest of any player on this list, having scored 113 of his 129 attempts.

For his current club, Bayern Munich, he has scored 41 of his 45 attempts from 12 yards, while for England, he has been successful with 26 of his 31 spot-kicks.

He isn't automatic from 12 yards, though. Of his 16 missed spot-kicks, his most famous came in England's defeat to France in the 2022 World Cup. He had the opportunity to equalise late in the quarter-final tie, but Kane blazed his effort over the bar, with England eventually losing 2-1. He also missed his first effort from 12 yards directly after winning the 2026 Ballon d'Or, hitting the bar against Borussia Dortmund that same week.

The striker has missed 16 penalties since 2001 and, despite a somewhat solid 79.7% conversion rate from the spot, he is in the top ten for most missed penalties in the 21st century. The Uruguayan was Napoli’s primary penalty taker, and although he scored the majority of his spot kicks for the Italian side, he did miss some crucial ones too.

Cavani, known for his poacher-like qualities, was never the designated penalty taker at Paris Saint-Germain. The 39-year-old had competition from world-class superstars such as Zlatan Ibrahimovic and Neymar in the early stints of his spell in France and this was before Kylian Mbappe had arrived in the French capital.

Likewise, at Manchester United, Cavani never took a penalty outside a shootout, and this was because of the presence of Cristiano Ronaldo, Bruno Fernandes, Anthony Martial and Marcus Rashford, who were all ahead of him in the spot-kick pecking order.

At his final club, Boca Juniors, he scored three of his five attempts from 12 yards.

Cristiano Ronaldo and David Beckham are just two stars who have worn Manchester United's most iconic shirt.

For as incredible as Kylian Mbappe is in front of goal, the fact he has missed from 12 yards on 16 occasions throughout his career is a huge surprise. His latest miss came when his stoppage-time spot-kick was saved in Real Madrid's 1-0 defeat against Real Betis in their La Liga clash in September 2026.

He will go down as one of the greatest goalscorers of all time, and maybe the fact he's trusted with penalty efforts for both club and country means he's bound to miss a fair few more than others around him.

Generally, you wouldn’t associate penalties with the former Barcelona and AC Milan man, but he was clearly trusted from the penalty spot.

Ronaldinho did in fact miss 16 penalties. However, three of these spot-kicks were taken before 2001 and therefore aren't included in this ranking. Despite converting most of his penalties, the ambitious playmaker made a name for himself for taking free kicks. Ronaldinho would often deploy an unusual but effective strategy, which entailed striking the ball underneath the wall rather than over or around it.

From Lionel Messi to Ronaldinho, there have been some incredible dribblers over the years.

Zlatan Ibrahimovic is a player who loves being in the spotlight. The Swede has scored some of the best goals in the most pressured situations, winning cups and leagues for a variety of different teams.

With that being said, Ibrahimovic took it upon himself to take penalties throughout his career and he stepped up to take 104 penalties. Despite this, the pressure of taking a penalty gets to even the best players at times and therefore his 17 penalty misses are more than understandable. Ibrahimovic, who retired at the age of 41, scored 87 goals from the penalty spot at an 83.6% conversion rate.

Football has had countless number nines over the years that have made a massive impact on the game, but who have been the best to ever wear the shirt?

Francesco Totti will go down as one of the best penalty-takers in the 21st century, yet he finds himself ranked highly on the list too. The striker scored so many goals during his playing days and, as expected, he has a conversion rate above 80%.

Amazingly, Totti didn’t miss a single penalty during his final four and a half seasons, converting 13 consecutive penalties at the back end of his career. The Italian did miss another two penalties in his career, but this was in 2001 and is therefore not counted in his tally. The versatile forward spent his entire career at Roma, winning the Serie A title, two Coppa Italia and two Supercoppa Italiana titles.

Immobile is best known for his spell at Lazio, where he holds the record as the club’s all-time top goalscorer. Furthermore, he also sits eighth on the all-time list of Serie A top goalscorers, which is another significant accomplishment for the striker.

The Italian missed 19 penalties in his career, which gives him an 81.9% conversion rate from 12 yards out. In August 2026, he decided to retire, so he won't have to worry about climbing any further up this list.

Neymar has stepped up to take penalties for club and country throughout his career and he has never shied away from this kind of pressure. The flamboyant winger will go down as one of the best takers of the modern generation, despite missing 22 penalties so far in his career.

Neymar has a slow run-up and typically goes for placement over power. The Brazilian has scored 97 penalties, which gives him a very respectable 81.5% conversion rate from the penalty spot. The 34-year-old has been the primary penalty taker for Paris Saint-Germain, Santos and the Brazil national team, while he took fewer penalties at Barcelona due to Lionel Messi being the main taker.

Where some players stand out for their physical qualities, others do so for their disconcerting agility.

Bologna coach Raffaele Palladino reveals he will punish Torbjorn Heggem for ‘over the top’ comments made on international duty by dropping him against Udinese, while there are injury updates.

“I don’t see first choice players, but I pick those who show me more in training. Dovbyk returned from international duty with a different spirit, he has made progress and I am pleased about that.”

#1320. Man United CEO Omar Berrada insists the team have IMPROVED since the transfer window in his first interview in five months - but does accept criticism of leadership has been fair

Published: 10:25 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 11:32 EST, 20 November 2026

Manchester United CEO Omar Berrada insists the team got 'fundamentally better' after this summer's transfer window, as he warned ‘spending just for the sake of it’ is not the route to putting United back on top.

In his first sit-down interview in five months, Berrada tackled topics ranging from the relationship between the Glazers and Ineos, the imminent departure of youngster JJ Gabriel, the decision not to sign a left back in the summer, as well as the decision to push ahead for a new stadium despite supporter backlash on matchdays.

The United chief has been at the centre of furious protests and anti-ownership chanting at matches this season, alongside Director of Football Jason Wilcox, and he accepted that criticism of United's leadership has, mostly, been fair.

In an interview that aired shortly after new head coach Mauricio Pochettino spoke to the media for the first time, Berrada was pressed on how much accountability falls at his door with United heading to Anfield this weekend 18th in the Premier League table.

'I think if you think about the fact we've had three permanent managers in less than three seasons, clearly we haven't achieved the stability that we wanted, that's for sure,' Berrada told Sky Sports.

'When it doesn't work out with the coach or the manager, we are all responsible. Myself, the football leadership, everyone who is involved around the coach and the staff and the players. We have to continue improving and getting better.

Manchester United's CEO Omar Berrada finally fronted up in an interview with Sky Sports

Michael Carrick's sacking was yet another managerial change at United, with the hierarchy under massive scrutiny and Mauricio Pochettino now in the hotseat

'There are different circumstances why it didn't work out with Erik [ten Hag], and Ruben [Amorim], and now Michael [Carrick], and we are always learning and, as I said, trying to improve and understand what has failed.

'The challenge is we're trying to find the right manager for the squad that we have with a specific set of skills in that moment to make them perform at their best level.

'It's true, we have to accept the criticism that we haven't been able to achieve that stability with one coach and our aim is to do that as soon as possible. Of course, we hope now that Mauricio coming in will give us that stability that I think we all need.'

Berrada's links to Manchester City, where he worked prior to joining United, were brought up, not least given he worked at the club during the period that City have had charges brought against them.

But at his new home there are issues aplenty, not least having got another managerial appointment wrong, sacking Carrick less than six months after handing him a two-year deal, and so it was put to Berrada: is the club actually progressing?

'It's not good enough, not acceptable and that's why we've made the change that we made so that we can move forward,' he concluded.

(L-R) Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Berrada and Jason Wilcox have drawn plenty of ire from Man United fans

'But we are laying the foundations for sustained growth, to put us in a position where we can be competitive consistently. It's not always been that.

'Last year we finished third, we were happy with the squad, we were happy with the way we were going. And now, a few months later, we are not where we need to be. But the foundations are there and I am convinced that we are heading in the right direction. Very positive.'

#1319. A new view of Amazonian leaf seasonality

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Gerbrand Koren is at the Copernicus Institute of Sustainable Development, Utrecht University, 3584 CB Utrecht, the Netherlands.

The Amazon rainforest plays a key part in the cycling of carbon and water on regional and global scales, and is widely viewed as a perennially evergreen ecosystem. However, writing in Nature, Song et al.1 report that there are extended periods when trees in most of the rainforest remain leafless. Known as deciduousness, this state occurs between the shedding of old leaves and the emergence and early development (flushing) of fresh ones. The authors also found that hydroclimatic conditions such as annual rainfall have a more crucial role in determining this pattern of leaf behaviour than do soil properties and light availability. The seasonal variation in tropical leaf cover and photosynthetic activity in the Amazon observed by the authors is less pronounced than that seen for broadleaf trees in temperate and boreal climate zones.

#1316. Tottenham Want to Sign Midfielder Yaya Fofana, Set to Watch Him Live

Tottenham will watch Stade de Reims star Yaya Fofana in action this weekend ahead of a possible transfer move, according to French outlet Foot Mercato.

Fofana has enjoyed a remarkable season for the Ligue 2 side and he will undoubtedly feature heavily in the headlines over the coming weeks following his goalscoring exploits as the January transfer window edges ever closer.

A versatile midfielder capable of playing in a number of positions, Fofana, who was recently called up to the Ivory Coast squad for the first time, has been utilised as an attacking midfielder by Reims boss Nicolas Usai this term and that has resulted in a real purple patch in front of goal.

Fofana has ten goals and three assists to his name from his 12 appearances this season, including nine goals in his last eight league games for his club side.

His form in the final third has come to the attention of Tottenham, with Foot Mercato reporting that the north London club will have people in the stands to watch the 22-year-old in action against St-Etienne on Saturday evening.

The French outlet report that Reims do not want to see their player leave during the January transfer window.

However, a permanent move with a six-month loan move back to Les rouges et blancs for the remainder of the season could well work for all parties concerned.

It is believed that a transfer away for Fofana would have to be in excess of the €25m (£21m) they recently received for Patrick Zabi following his move to Paris FC in the summer.

So what exactly would Fofana bring to Tottenham?

Well, Roberto De Zerbi would certainly be inheriting a very talented player and one that can play in a number of positions.

Fofana's ability to play further forward and flourish in the final third has been evident this season after so far amassing ten goals in 12 league appearances for Reims.

"Yaya is an instinctive player, so you have to give him a lot of freedom," said Usai, as reported by Morning Foot.

"He is able to play in a double pivot in the fairly low middle, he is able to play playmaker, he is able to play attacker, he is able to play on one side."

He added: "It's a talented player, but I insist that it's really an instinctive profile, so he must be left free.

"Of course he has defensive instructions and that he must tune defensively in the service of the collective, but when he has the ball or when he is able to dezone, the partners simply need to be able to adjust their movement."

On the prospect of losing his player in January, Usai said: "No, no, no fear. Really, it's early November, so I don't ask myself that kind of question."

Spurs will look to complete at least two transfers when the January transfer window opens

#1315. How Mo Salah Has Achieved Incredible Ripped Physique in His 30s

Mohamed Salah has been known to keep his body in peak physical condition throughout his football career. Having turned 34 years old in June 2026, this is even more vital than ever before if the 'Egyptian King' plans to extend his stay at the top of the beautiful game for years to come.

The likes of Cristiano Ronaldo and even Salah's former Liverpool teammate, James Milner, notably continued playing at the highest level into their late 30s after taking extreme care of their bodies over the years.

These football stars shocked everyone by getting into even better shape after quitting the game...

He returned to pre-season training ahead of the 2024/25 campaign and blew the competition out of the water when it came to running tests, despite being one of the few experienced players back at the training ground at the time. Salah was even called 'phenomenal' by a member of Liverpool's coaching staff upon his return from holiday.

Fast-forward to 2026 – having left Liverpool in the summer – the 34-year-old joined Trabzonspor. His commitment to fitness has kept him in good form in Turkey so far. Beyond the football, though, he also caused a stir online when he shared an image of his impressive six-pack on social media.

According to the Daily Mail, a huge part of Salah's secret to being in such fine physical shape is his diet. The Egypt international has his own personal chef, who is tasked with preparing all the right foods to keep the winger firing on all cylinders.

It's claimed that he eats broccoli with almost every single meal, along with other 'superfoods'. This is just part of his recipe for success. The Liverpool icon is also extremely fond of a dish from his home country, called koshary, which is a mixture of fried rice, pasta, pulses, onions and tomato sauce.

In 2022, he went into more detail about what his favourite foods are and even spoke about what he likes to eat when treating himself. Even then, however, it's clear how health-conscious he is:

"I prefer broccoli, sweet potatoes, fish, chicken and always salad. When I indulge in a great restaurant in London, I prefer sushi. I eat pizza once a month at the most. I love hamburgers, but I hardly ever eat them because afterwards I feel heavy!"

As well as his healthy eating, he also looks after his body 24/7 in other ways. Inside his home, Salah has two different gym rooms along with some incredible equipment that helps to keep him fit. He's said to have a hyperbaric chamber in his house, which aims to help the lungs spread more oxygen around the body by having air pressure levels three times higher than normal conditions.

He also has cryotherapy facilities which include ice-led machines which constrict blood vessels to decrease swelling. It's incredible to see the lengths Salah goes to when it comes to his training regime. As a Muslim, the forward has to adapt his routine during Ramadan, which includes 2am gym sessions.

GIVEMESPORT Key Statistic: Mohamed Salah is the top goalscorer in Premier League history for Liverpool, having eclipsed Robbie Fowler's tally of 128 in 2023.

Having defined the very best moments of the Jurgen Klopp years, he began a new era at the Merseyside-based club by scoring and assisting on the opening day of the 2024/25 Premier League season against Ipswich Town in what was Arne Slot's first competitive game in charge.

Despite his brilliant form in 2024/25, there were doubts about Salah's future as his contract was due to run out in 2025. But, thankfully for Liverpool fans around the world, the club and Salah were able to agree to a deal as he put pen to paper on a new two-year contract in April 2025.

The 30 greatest players in Liverpool history have been named, including Steven Gerrard, Kenny Dalglish, Virgil van Dijk and Mohamed Salah.

Despite putting pen to paper on a deal until 2027, Salah announced that he'd be cutting that contract short and departing at the end of the 2025-26 season. He then joined Trabzonspor in the summer of 2026, signing a two-year contract in August. It took him until just September to score his first hat-trick for his new side, doing so against defending champions Galatasaray.

Still fit and firing at 34, it just goes to show how well Salah has looked after his body.

#1314. McInnes wants a quiet January... but it might just be the right time for Rangers to cash in on Raskin

Published: 11:37 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 11:44 EST, 20 November 2026

Derek McInnes can be understood in wanting a quiet January window. He’s still bonding a squad of players together. Drama and diversions are the last thing he needs when there looks to be an opportunity to win a title on the horizon.

In the case of Olwethu Makhanya, for example, this is definitely not the time to sell.

The 22-year-old South African has been impressive at centre-back, but it will take a campaign catching the attention in high-level European football for him to raise his value to Calvin Bassey levels and beyond.

Same goes for the likes of Ryan Naderi. Getting into the Czechia squad and increasing his range of experience makes him a more interesting prospect, but UEFA competition is a platform that ought to increase his premium.

McInnes, as he did this week, has to say he wants to keep his more prominent talents anyway. It would be strange to appear accepting of the board cashing in on bigger players.

When it comes to Nico Raskin, however, things are different. A buyer for him should have been found in the summer after his World Cup involvement with Belgium.

Rangers midfielder Nico Raskin is an asset who could be sold in the January transfer window

From the chit-chat around the game, it does not seem unreasonable to think Rangers maybe overvalued him in the initial part of that window and missed the boat in terms of securing a sale.

If he stays for the rest of this season and enters the final year of his contract, though, the money you can ask for naturally reduces. The club might seek to tie him up on a new deal, of course, but his remarks about being ‘mentally ready to leave’ at the start of the season point to the most likely direction of travel.

Is he irreplaceable? Not at all. And this is where forward planning should come into the mix.

If there’s someone out there willing to edge anywhere close to the £15m mark for the 25-year-old, they should be getting sounded out now – with a contingency plan being discussed and worked on in tandem.

Yes, Rangers need to get back to winning silverware, but the need to start raising funds through selling players – and replacing them - at appropriate times is pressing too.

As often said here, they can’t keep spending money the way they have been without considerably more coming back in return.

Raskin’s a good player, but his three-and-a-half years at Ibrox have hardly been shaped by his propensity for winning medals, have they? If a realistic fee is there in January, there’s a case to make for it being taken.

#1313. Conte: ‘Chelsea did not want Terry, so my wife made him pasta’

Antonio Conte reveals how his wife made pasta for John Terry and changed the course of his Chelsea career. ‘The club had no intention of renewing his contract, he wasn’t even mentioned.’

The Italian tactician sat down with podcast Cronache di Spogliatoio and looked back over his long experience in Italy and England, including the Premier League title and FA Cup at Stamford Bridge from 2016 to 2018.

He explained that Terry’s playing career could’ve been so very different, as before he became a legend for the London club, he was about to be pushed out of the door.

“Terry was a fundamental figure in our Premier League title victory,” said Conte.

“A solid guy, he flew with a private jet along with his agent from London to see me in Turin. His contract was running down, he decided to pay for the flight to visit me.

“He basically said I love Chelsea so much that I want to keep going. Until that day, we had never talked about Terry. Marina Abramovich said he wanted to come and talk to me, but they had no intention of renewing his contract.

“My wife ended up making pasta for John Terry and his agent, who I had not met before. I assured him, I don’t care about how old you are, but if you prove that you deserve to play in training, then I will play you.

“The only promise you have to make is that even if you don’t play, you are still added value in the locker room, because you represent the history of this club.”

At that time, Terry was 35 years old and Conte confirms Chelsea had not the slightest intention of keeping him in the squad, ready to let him leave as a free agent.

“He simply wasn’t mentioned, that was the season when they finished 10th. I’d met all the Chelsea players a month earlier, but they didn’t let me meet Terry, because he just wasn’t on their radar,” added the coach.

Conte also reveals how Terry represented the Chelsea squad prompting a complaint for his very Italian way of working, which at the time seemed unusual to Premier League players.

“Terry came to me in training one day and said the players felt we were doing too much tactical work, too many videos. When my captain comes and tells me that, I have to speak to the staff and move towards them.

“It might be a coincidence, but after that we drew with Swansea, lost to Arsenal, so I thought we’re going back to my approach. If we have to die, we die with my ideas,” insisted Conte.

“The dressing room was bubbling up, ready to revolt, but then after another break, Terry comes to me. ‘Hey gaffer, we’ve got to keep doing the tactical stuff, because these things actually happened during the game!’

“They realised he’s not just telling us things for no reason, they are situations you see in the match, and that changed everything,” concluded Conte.

#1312. Meet ‘egoviruses’: the surprise microbes living in the guts of millions of people

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Rachel Fieldhouse is a reporter for Nature in Sydney, Australia.

Many giant viruses can be seen under a light microscope.Credit: Gabrielle Voinot/Eurelios/Look at Sciences/SPL

Roughly 180 million people could be carrying previously unknown giant viruses inside their guts. Microbiologists say that these ‘egoviruses’ could be the missing link between giant viruses that infect single-celled organisms and distantly related poxviruses, such as those that cause smallpox and mpox, which can infect people and animals directly. The findings are published in Nature1.

Large and giant viruses in the phylum Nucleocytoviricota are a vast group of DNA viruses — some are so big that they can be seen under a light microscope — that mostly infect single-celled organisms in the environment.

Poxviruses are an outlier in the giant-virus world because they can directly infect humans and animals and their origin is a mystery, says Fasséli Coulibaly, a structural biologist at Monash University in Melbourne, Australia. Egoviruses could be the evolutionary bridge between microorganism-infecting giant viruses called asfuviruses and pathogenic poxviruses, he says.

Tom Delmont, a microbial ecologist at the French National Centre for Scientific Research in Paris, and his colleagues discovered egoviruses while combing through online libraries of metagenomes. These contain the genetic information of all the organisms in a particular environment, which means that researchers can hunt for microbes without having to cultivate them. When the team scanned for a single gene found in most nucleocytoviruses, they discovered egoviruses — the only type of nucleocytovirus that is prevalent in the gut.

They found egovirus DNA in gut samples from people, buffalo, goats, chickens, deer and pigs. Six clades were unique to people. One of these clades is estimated to be present in roughly 1% of the global population, on the basis of the presence of at least one of two egovirus proteins in the samples they analysed.

The researchers detected these proteins in samples spanning a large proportion of the human population, from the Hadza, a hunter-gatherer group in Tanzania, to populations in Europe, the United States and South America, says Delmont. That suggests that egoviruses have been inhabiting the human gut for a long time, he adds.

That egoviruses are found in many animal species, including people, and are widespread around the world shows that giant viruses are more diverse than previously thought, says Subir Sarker, a molecular virologist at James Cook University in Townsville, Queensland. “This is a really groundbreaking study,” he adds.

To identify potential hosts for egoviruses in the gut, the team compared the amount of genetic overlap between egoviruses and organisms with a nucleus. The researchers found the most overlap with single-celled organisms that help ruminants, such as cows, to digest their food.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03766-w

#1311. Saliba has fight on his hands to usurp ‘unbelievable’ Konsa

From the moment Ezri Konsa pulled on an Arsenal shirt, he has moved with all the composure of a man who knows exactly where to be and when. The centre-back has required no adaptation period in north London, where he has filled the considerable shoes of William Saliba with such class that Arsenal have hardly missed the Frenchman at all.

The loss of Saliba to a long-term back injury was supposed to be a major problem for Arsenal. Instead, the situation has now reached a point where some fans are wondering how Saliba will get back into the side. That may prove a little extreme, but the fact there is even a discussion is proof of Konsa’s superb impact at the Emirates Stadium.

“Unbelievable,” Mikel Arteta, the Arsenal manager, said of his £55m signing. “He’s come to a huge club and to position yourself in that manner, and to perform at the level he is, it is very difficult to do. We are really lucky to have him.”

In Arsenal’s latest victory, their seventh from eight matches in the Premier League this season, Konsa offered all of his usual defensive security and calmness in possession. Even more excitingly, he also scored his first goal for the club, smashed in from close range after a corner had caused chaos in Everton’s penalty area. It was Arsenal’s first set-piece goal of the season.

“I have been waiting to score my first goal for a while,” Konsa said. “I spoke to the set-piece coach before the game and he told me he’s been waiting for my goal as well. We felt as players that it was coming, and today was the day.”

Some eyebrows were raised when Arsenal paid such a large fee to sign Konsa from Aston Villa. The Villa fans, though, were not among those who questioned the price or the player’s ability. They have known for years at Villa Park that Konsa is a player of the highest quality, and they will not be surprised by his exceptional start to his Arsenal career.

The same is true of the Arsenal players. Arteta asked the England internationals in his squad about Konsa before buying him, and the feedback was overwhelmingly positive. Konsa was already close friends with Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze before completing his transfer from Villa.

Konsa’s start to life at Arsenal is all the more impressive because he did not even have a pre-season. He effectively came straight from the World Cup into the club, and has been starting games since early September. His first start was against Chelsea, when he endeared himself to the home fans with a crunching tackle on former team-mate Morgan Rogers.

Konsa, 29, has quickly built a strong relationship with Gabriel Magalhães, his defensive partner who scored Arsenal’s other goal here against Everton, from Ben White’s cross. For both centre-backs to find the net felt like a throwback to last year, when Arsenal were so dangerous from crosses, and underlined how Arteta’s team are capable of hurting their opponents in many different ways.

The nature of the goals might give a misleading impression of Arsenal’s performance, though. This was not a gritty win. Arteta’s side produced some excellent passing moves and circulated the ball with menace throughout the game. They were also a little open at times, especially in the first half when Everton created a handful of decent chances.

Thierno Barry missed the best of those opportunities, with the score at 1-0. It was the closest the visitors came to hurting the champions, aside from some of James Tarkowski’s full-blooded tackles. “I felt we didn’t really get to a level that was good enough to get near them,” admitted David Moyes, the Everton manager.

The victory, combined with Manchester City’s defeat earlier in the day, put Arsenal level on points at the top of the table. Aside from the extraordinary thrashing at Brighton, Arteta’s side have looked just as solid, if not more so, than last season. That speaks volumes of the quality in the team, of course, but also says plenty about the way Konsa has adjusted to his new surroundings. Thanks to him, Saliba’s absence has not hurt at all.

“Great feeling, it always is. A clean sheet, a goal – my first goal for the club – so a fantastic day overall.

“I’ve been waiting to score my first goal for a while. I spoke to the set piece coach before the game and he told me he’s been waiting for my goal as well, so it was only right that I got the goal today.

“I’ve come to this stadium for many seasons, I know how tough it is to play against us. It’s not surprising to me.

“We are champions and to be champions you’ve got to win games consistently. This is our home and we want to win as many games here as possible.”

All over at the Emirates and the champions go level on points with Manchester City at the top of the table.

They kept another clean sheet and scored from a set-piece again. All is right in Arsenal’s world!

Oscar Bobb’s first Premier League goal for Fulham earned a 1-0 win over Coventry that lifted the Cottagers clear of the relegation zone.

Bobb produced a fine bit of individual skill to strike in the 80th minute as he twisted his way into the box and bent a shot into the far corner, only his second goal for the club in any competition since his £27million move from Manchester City back in January.

That was enough to give Fulham their first away win in nine attempts, a run that dated back to February, only a week after they ended their winless start to the league campaign by edging out Hull 1-0 as the pressure continues to ease on Alvaro Arbeloa.

Josh King had earlier hit the post for the visitors, who edged Coventry in just about every department to leave Frank Lampard’s side second-bottom of the table.

The hosts had only brief spells of sustained possession in Fulham’s half, but did little to trouble Bernd Leno on a frustrating afternoon which bought the CBS Arena back down to earth after their 4-1 win over Newcastle in their last home outing.

Odegaard drives a shot high over the ball as Arsenal close in on another clean sheet.

Brilliant play from Oscar Bobb as he cuts inside on his left foot and bends a shot into the far bottom corner for the away side.

Arsenal have found their groove again, with Madueke twice going close to extending their lead. Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Odegaard and Merino are forming a box in midfield and Everton don’t seem to know how to shut them down.

Everton have responded well to going behind here. The early goal against them will have ripped up any plans to sit deep and play on the counter.

Set-pieces are back on the menu for Arsenal. Ezri Konsa’s first goal for the club is their first goal from a corner this season, which will come as a relief to set-piece coach Nicolas Jover. “Set piece again, ole ole,” sing the Arsenal fans. Arteta’s side had started the game on the front foot.

Arsenal had not scored from a corner this season... until now. Konsa breaks the deadlock after a melee in the box and his pokes the ball into the net.

A couple of early set pieces from Declan Rice. Everton do well to clear the danger. But have another one now...

Horrible conditions at the Emirates today. The rain has been lashing down. The Emirates drainage system is usually able to cope with this sort of thing. If the wind picks up, that’s likely to be a bigger problem for the two teams.

After a minute’s applause in honour of Ken Friar, the match makes a prompt start at the Emirates.

“Yeah, we’ve had a good start. Obviously, we had a bit of a blip last week against Chelsea. I don’t think we, as a team, won first and second balls enough and that’s something the manager wants us to get back to today. You’ve got to win your battles.”

On what makes Arsenal difficult to play...

“They’re reigning Premier League champions, a top side that has been knocking on the door to win the title for a few years before as well. They’re a team at a high level but this is what Premier League football is all about and it’s up to us to get a result.”

“Well, we play every two-and-a-half days so we didn’t have much time to recover, so we need full energy. There are certain specific players as well that they fit really well for the game that we expect today and that’s how we start.”

“A very competitive team, a really well organised team. I think that it’s very clear what they want to do, where they want to take the game. The threats, when they have a space to run, any time that they are able to put the ball in their box, you know the presence and aggression that they have. So, yeah, we have to really be at it and be very aggressive from the beginning.”

One of the clearest signs a football club is in a good place is when the debate switches from whether the team are winning to how they are winning.

This is currently Arsenal and Mikel Arteta’s world. For years, Arsenal coaches and players were asked how and when they would start collecting major trophies again. With no concern about their capacity to challenge for top honours over the coming years, the style has become the main focus.

It’s a welcome “problem” – or some might argue a non-existent one – for Arteta while his side is so strong. Building a fortress is the expensive, time-consuming and difficult part. Once it’s constructed and established, how you decorate it is a matter of taste.

Whether neutrals will hold the current champions in the same regard as the great Arsène Wenger sides will be a trivial concern if Arteta does what no Arsenal manager has since 1935 – defend the league title – and then add a few more, which is a serious possibility based on the balance of power in England and the likely punishment heading Manchester City’s way.

Today there will be tributes to Ken Friar, who passed away at the age of 92 earlier this year. Advertising boards outside the Emirates Stadium have been taken over by images of Friar, who had a remarkable 70-year association with the club.

In today’s programme, captain Martin Odegaard has written the following: “It’s exceptional people like Ken Friar who have built the club into what it is today, and we as the current team are the ones privileged to continue his legacy.”

This is a first Premier League start of the season for Viktor Gyokeres, who has been behind Kai Havertz in the pecking order over the past few months. Gyokeres has yet to score in nine appearances in all competitions this season, although he would (understandably) make the point that it’s harder to do so when you are coming off the bench late in games.

For Arsenal, Arteta shuffles his team after the draw against Bayern: White, Lewis-Skelly, Merino, Eze and Gyokeres start.

Max Dowman, who scored a memorable goal in this fixture last season, is on the bench.

For Everton, Jack Grealish misses today’s game due to sickness, while Jarrad Branthwaite is absent because of concussion protocols despite finishing last week’s match with Chelsea after a head collision with Emi Martinez.

Arsenal: Raya, White, Gabriel, Konsa, Lewis-Skelly, Rice, Merino, Odegaard, Madueke, Eze, Gyokeres.Subs: Arrizabalaga, Timber, Hincapie, Calafiori, Mosquera, Zubimendi, Guimaraes, Dowman, Havertz

Hello and welcome to coverage from the Emirates as Premier League champions Arsenal host Everton.

Mikel Arteta’s men produced a good performance in midweek to draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League while David Moyes’s squad have had the week off following their 2-0 defeat by Chelsea last weekend.

Arteta said: “We’re having three games in six days so we know what’s happening, especially when the games are so demanding and the necessity is to win. We know that, so we prepare the players for those scenarios and do the best we possibly can.

“I know David so well and how he sets the team, the quality they have in their organisation and individually. It’s no coincidence they didn’t lose before their last game. They have a really good team, which we know because in recent clashes, it’s always been a really difficult game for us.”

Both teams enter this game having been beaten just once this season but eight points separate them with Arsenal in second and Everton in eighth.

Moyes said: “It’s not an easy game and never has been over many years. We look forward to it; they had a game in midweek, and we have to try and capitalise on that. I thought we did really well last year against them; we played really well down at Arsenal, and I hope we can do the same.

“When I look back at the team we had out, we were pretty threadbare at that time, but we did a good job, and I hope we can do it again. Obviously Arsenal have some many different tools in their bag and people they can use in different positions, so we’re fully aware of the team we’re up against and the level.”

Former Arsenal players Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Christian Norgaard could feature for Everton this afternoon.

#1310. Milan priority is to lock Rabiot down to new improved contract

Milan patron Gerry Cardinale held a meeting at the club headquarters today to discuss the transfer strategy, but the priority is to lock down Adrien Rabiot to a new and improved contract.

The RedBird chief has been very hands-on with the Serie A side this season, having vented his frustration at missing out on a Champions League spot last term by cleaning house.

According to Sky Sport Italia, Cardinale was present at the club headquarters this afternoon for a series of meetings with various directors, as they begin to set out the plans for January.

The main priority, however, is to lock down the talent in the squad right now, and that means ensuring France international Rabiot signs a new contract.

The 31-year-old is already tied to the San Siro giants until June 2028, with an option to extend, but that is considered insufficient for his importance to Ruben Amorim’s team.

Rabiot contributed five goals and as many assists in 13 competitive appearances for Milan so far this season, and his absence was sorely felt whenever there was rotation to let him rest.

It is believed the new contract will run to June 2030, with an improved salary of €5m per season plus performance-related bonuses, compared to his current €3.5m.

Meanwhile, the Rossoneri are also ready to announce the arrival of new Head of Football Markus Krosche over the next few days, once the final details have been resolved.

#1309. Drone operator apologises for filming Mauricio Pochettino's first training session, while Man United must apply to close airspace if they want to avoid another embarrassing security breach

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER

Published: 04:54 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 13:58 EST, 20 November 2026

The drone operator who filmed Mauricio Pochettino’s first training session at Manchester United has removed the video from his YouTube account and apologised to the club.

United suffered the embarrassing security breach on Pochettino’s first day as head coach after the 12-minute footage showing the Argentine and his staff working with the players at Carrington was posted online.

The owner of the account called CC Overview, who is known only as Colin, justified the intrusion by saying that the airspace over Carrington is unrestricted and the drone was operating legally within Civil Aviation Authority rules.

United will have to apply to the Department of Transport if they want to close off the airspace to avoid more unwanted drones.

CC Overview took the video down on Friday morning insisting that he was unaware of the significance of his actions.

He also clarified that neither Liverpool – who are United’s opponents in Pochettino’s first game at Anfield on Sunday – nor any other club were involved in the filming.

Mauricio Pochettino's first Man United training session was filmed by a drone and the operator has now apologised

The drone user, who is known only as Colin, said he had not broken laws but apologised

United have declined to comment over the incident and it’s unclear if the club have made contact with him or involved Greater Manchester Police.

His statement read: ‘I would like to speak about yesterday’s incident. A total error of judgement on my part led to me filming some of the Manchester United training session at Carrington, whilst the flight was legal in terms of drone laws I fully accept it was unethical on my part.

‘My aim was to picture Mauricio Pochettino in his United training kit for the supporters to see for the first time.

'I had wrongly presumed that with it being close to the start of the session that no meaningful training sessions would have started so would have been some harmless warming up shown.

‘I also wrongly assumed that the training session would have been open to various media outlets.

'I would like to apologise to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino and the players for my actions and sincerely hope those actions do not affect the outcome of any match. I would also like to state that Liverpool Football club or any other football club were not involved in my decision to film at Carrington yesterday.

‘The video has been removed from my channel. I have spent the past four years building up my YouTube channel and were well regarded in the fields I film and would now like to get back to building up my damaged reputation and making well received responsible videos. Thank you.’

United say they will not pursue legal action this time but will not hesitate to do so if it happens in the future.

To stop drones legally flying over Carrington, it has emerged that the club would need to seek permission from the Government to restrict the airspace around the training ground.

Footage of the session was captured close to Carrington and uploaded online

There are tight controls issued by the CAA and National Air Traffic Services over flying drones of different sizes, and a code of conduct related to how they are operated. It includes sharing photos and videos that could be ‘unfair’ to anyone.

It states that drones over 250g should not be flown closer than 50 metres to people, and drones below that weight should not be flown over crowds.

The drone and model aircraft code also states that you must ‘keep at least 150m away from residential, recreational, commercial and industrial areas’. It lists sports facilities as a recreational area.

Man United installed signs in 2018 warning that the use of drones over Carrington was 'strictly prohibited' and would be reported for prosecution

‘Think before sharing photos and videos. Avoid sharing anything that could be unfair or harmful to anyone. Think carefully about who could see your photos and videos – especially before posting them on social media. Apply the same common-sense approach that you would with images or video recorded on a smartphone or digital camera.’

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola was asked about the drone on Friday, saying: 'It shouldn't be legal. There is a reason why we train behind closed doors. It's not nice for any club.'

#1308. Conte: ‘I would love to join an organised club, rather than always adding value’

Antonio Conte insists he would love ‘before ending my career to take over a club that is already organised’ after years of ‘building value’ from troubled situations like Juventus, Chelsea, Inter and Napoli.

The coach is currently between jobs after walking away from Napoli in two years where he won the Serie A title and the Supercoppa Italiana.

There were reports he could come to Manchester United or even return to his old side Juve, but he is in no rush for his next role.

Speaking to the Cronache di Spogliatoio podcast, Conte did outline his greatest strength, and why he perhaps eager to cast it aside and do something different next time.

“There is one thing I’d love to do before ending my career as a coach, which is to take over a club that is already organised,” said Conte.

“It would be like stepping into a Formula 1 car in pole position. It never happened in my career, but evidently that is just the way it goes for me. I always arrived at complicated situations and was fortunate, but also deserve credit, for taking a team back to victory.

“Often, it involved returning them to their history, a dimension that perhaps they had forgotten.”

It all sounds like the scenario at Manchester United, who have not won the Premier League since 2013, following in the footsteps of other clubs he went through.

“It happened at Juventus, who got back to winning after seven years, Inter hadn’t won the Scudetto for 10, and Chelsea were coming off a disastrous season when I arrived, finishing in 10th place, but then won the Premier League with me.

“The same was true at Napoli, where they had finished 10th, then I arrived and took them to victory.”

That also means Conte brings with him certain expectations, something he is quick to point out in press conferences from the very start.

“It is inevitable that when you arrive with a curriculum like this, you are accompanied by big expectations. People and the media expect you to win. I still remember when I arrived at Napoli, a team that finished 10th, a beautiful city, their objective was to qualify for the Champions League.

“I thought I could just enjoy my work and the city for a while, but the moment I signed, the media completely changed the message. I don’t know how many other coaches would be treated that way.”

In fairness, Napoli had won the Scudetto the previous season under Luciano Spalletti, then limped to 10th place after going through a series of coaches, but retained much the same team.

When it comes to Inter, Conte also argues he laid the foundations for all those who followed him.

“I arrived and the Appiano Gentile ground was disastrous, the pitches had big holes in, there was always an alibi from the staff. Inter invested in revamping the pitch, and a month later it was ruined again,” said the coach.

“The club spent €120,000 and in those two years, I also asked for them to set up somewhere to sleep. If you look at the Inter training ground today, it is a gem.

“There are many clubs where there is a before me, and an after me, and those who come later find this.”

Conte also discussed the player sales that sides like Inter made thanks to his development of certain players.

“I become an investment for clubs that pays off. We signed Romelu Lukaku and Achraf Hakimi, then sold them on for €120m to Chelsea and €70m to PSG. I added value to the squad.”

The England back row, never knowingly far from controversy, escalated a brawl at the end of the first half that Leicester prop Joe Heyes revealed “added fuel to the fire” of a Tigers side who roared impressively when they returned after the break.

The incident fired up a sell-out crowd and Leicester brought what had up to that point been a drab game to life with a storming second-half performance.

“We got on the front foot and showed our power. The way the guys problem-solved was brilliant and I’m just really pleased with the emotional energy they threw into that game.

“The way we were physically for each other – I’m really pleased.

“The challenge for us, if we want to be a title-winning team, is to play like that when it isn’t Northampton Saints. We have to play with that heart – the fire we showed in our chests – but also the calmness we showed too.

“I think if we play our game to the best of our ability we can knock over anyone.”

They come again but the Tigers lose it through Chessum five-metres out - it’s a very wet ball out there so we can expect to see a lot of that - and Pollock leads the celebrations among the forwards. You can bet he’ll be in their faces all afternoon.

Saints strike first! They make a mess of their first line out but Chessum manages to knock on and the visitors have a scrum in Tigers’ 22. The hosts are too eager to engage and Mitchell takes the free kick quickly. Saints edge forward with some patient phase play - they get the offside advantage and Smith chips the Tigers’ defence.

Billy Searle is tracking the ball but he’s scampering back awkwardly and completely misses the catch. Instead James Pater gathers the loose ball and watches it into his hands.. and grounds it. Saints strike first! Conversion is good.

Billy Searle gets proceedings underway and its Saints who gain some fine field position early on after the hosts are penalised for not rolling away. .. and enter what looks like a horrendously wet Welford Road. Rain is pouring - expect dropped balls and greasy conditions!

Our rugby reporter Charles Richardson relieves the time Manu Tuilagi gave one - or a few - to Chris Ashton back in 2011.

In a fiery – when is this fixture not? – first half, both were sin-binned for their involvement in what might be described as a disagreement.

Tuilagi took Ashton out, slightly high, off the ball as the wing attempted to support scrum-half Lee Dickson’s quickly taken penalty. Ashton then gave the 19-year-old, uncapped Tuilagi a little shove on the floor, before the red mist descended on the future England centre. Catch the full read here.

Henry Pollock’s cornrow phase is over. He’s sporting a mousy mop for today’s East Midlands derby.

The Northampton No 8 - currently warming up in a snood - will be pantomime-villain-in-chief for the Saints in these parts but he has a big afternoon ahead.

This is exactly the sort of occasion and arm wrestle which he needs to excel in to prove to Steve Borthwick he is worth more than a bench role for England next month.

Wrapped up against the storm ⛈️ It's wet and windy ahead of the East Midlands derby - just ask Henry Pollock! 😅 📺 Stream TNT Sports on HBO Max https://t.co/ISqfkeU3vl https://t.co/1pirJ1Nm2D

Leicester were buoyed in the week by re-signing Jack van Poortfliet, who extended his contract with his boyhood club.

I grew up supporting Leicester, it’s always been my club,” said the England scrum half. This place feels like home in my rugby life. The club is in a really good position, I think we have a great group of lads and great coaches.

I love playing rugby here, I have my best mates here and I believe that we’ve got a group of lads that we can do great things with. I want to be in a place that I love playing for and I believe can win trophies.”

Squally conditions this afternoon at Mattioli Welford Road - in fact make that horrible. An interesting test then for Northampton as lovers of the beautiful game.

You would imagine that the rain and wind would suit a Leicester side whose DNA is set piece power better.

Expect the catch and drive to get plenty of game time and Jack van Poortvliet and Billy Searle to go to the air regularly. It could be a stern examination for teenage Saints full-back James Pater.

It’s a big day for Alex Coles, who celebrates his milestone 150th cap today.

The 27-year-old lock follows Fraser Dingwall, Rory Hutchinson and Alex Mitchell to become the fourth member of Saints’ current squad to reach 150 appearances for his boyhood club, eight years after making his debut in 2018.

Coles marks one of nine changes to Saints’ side for the Derby Day clash, with Emmanuel Iyogun, Curtis Langdon, Ed Prowse, Tom Pearson and Henry Pollock the other names coming into the forward pack.

Cleopas Kundiona retains his place in the front row while milestone man Coles joins Prowse in the second row against Tigers.

Josh Kemeny, with the 27-year-old continues at blindside flanker while Tom Pearson is set to make his first Prem appearance of the season.

Northampton Saints: J Pater; T Freeman, R Hutchinson, F Dingwall, G Hendy; F Smith, A Mitchell, E Iyogun, C Langdon, C Kundiona, A Coles, E Prowse, J Kemeny, T Pearson, H Pollock.

Replacements: R Smith, D Fischetti, I Neculai, JJ Van Der Mescht, T Lockett, C Chick, A McParland, O Sleightholme.

Parling has made five changes from the side that endured a 41-17 defeat to Pau.

Solomone Kata returns from injury to start at inside centre, with Gabriel Hamer-Webb and Jack van Poortvliet also coming into the backline to replace Ollie Hassell-Collins and Tom Whiteley respectively.

In the pack, Joe Heyes joins Archie van der Flier and Jamie Blamire who retain their places in the front row, while the second row make up of Cameron Henderson and Ollie Chessum remains unchanged.

Aaron Wainwright comes back into the starting lineup in the back row, with Finn Carnduff moving to openside flanker, with Olly Cracknell going at No 8.

Leicester: F Steward; A Radwan, W Wand, S Kata; G Hamer-Webb; B Searle, J van Poortvliet; A van der Flier, J Blamire, J Heyes, C Henderson, O Chessum, A Wainwright, F Carnduff, O Cracknell.

Replacements:  R Asiata, T Haffar, W Hurd, J Thompson, J Moro, T Whiteley, O Bailey, G Pearson.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of Leicester Tigers v Northampton Saints.

The Prem’s derby weekend continues today at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, where Geoff Parling’s side go head-to-head in with their East Midlands rivals.

Both Leicester and Northampton have two wins from the opening three rounds of the season and with both sides involved in a number of high-scoring encounters already in the new campaign, we could be in for a real treat.

Tigers started the season with a 38-40 loss at home to Saracens, but bounced back quickly with wins over Gloucester and Newcastle Red Bulls. They will be itching to right a few wrongs after suffering a chastening Champions Cup defeat in Pau last week.

Northampton, meanwhile, have notched up wins over Newcastle Red Bulls and Bath either side of loss to Bristol Bears.

A win today for Saints would be their first on the road since defeating Exeter Chiefs at Sandy Park in April.

“It (the East Midlands derby) means a lot to everyone, we know it will be a great atmosphere at Mattioli Woods Welford Road,” said Parling.

“I don’t think with this sort of game either team has to build it up too much emotionally because that just comes, so I think it’s actually about being really really calm in the moment.”

“Hopefully we can put the best of ourselves out there and I’m sure Saints will be able to do exactly the same.”

Saints are without a victory in Leicester since January 2023, when a single point decided the 18-19 result.

Since then, the last five meetings between the sides have been won by the hosts on the day – with Saints last taking home the bragging rights when a Tom Litchfield hat-trick helped Northampton to a 45-31 win on home soil in last season’s league play-off.

Kick-off gets underway at 3.05pm. Stay with us here for all the latest updates.

#1305. Donnarumma praise from Maresca and Hart after Italy and Manchester City criticism

Italy international Gianluigi Donnarumma received criticism lately, but Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca and former goalkeeper Joe Hart rushed to his defence.

The shot-stopper was guilty of a few howlers for the Azzurri in the Nations League, most notably in the 3-1 victory over France, but also made a series of big saves over the two matches.

He will be suspended for the next Italy match in 2027, although that will not be in the Nations League after finishing third in the group behind France and Belgium.

“He has been good,” assured Manchester City coach Maresca with regards to Donnarumma.

“I think with the international team, he made a mistake in the build-up. But in Italy he was the man of the match in the game, he made many good saves.

“We made some mistakes in the last games. Gigi was part of that. He is aware. Hopefully he’s not going to make any more mistakes. He is going to start against Fulham.”

Former Manchester City, Torino and England goalkeeper Hart has also used his column on the official City website to heap praise upon the Italian, who only recently won the Champions League at Paris Saint-Germain.

Donnarumma also won the Yashin Trophy, the goalkeeper’s equivalent of the Ballon d’Or, twice.

“I think some of Gianluigi’s performances were breathtaking, absolutely astonishing. He’s the captain of Italy. Simply put, he’s at the top table of goalkeepers,” wrote Hart.

“I think he’s proven his quality and his ability on numerous occasions since joining City. Yes he’s not had the best couple of months but that’s the life of a goalkeeper. He’ll have experienced it before. He’ll experience it again. We shouldn’t forget all the brilliant stuff he does for the team.”

Hart praised Donnarumma’s role in the locker room too, noting he is “a really beautiful human being” and “renowned for his hugs.”

#1304. Sensational Spurs storm Stamford Bridge as Palmer loses his head

So much for Xabi Alonso’s call for cool heads from his Chelsea players. Cole Palmer lost his and was sent off, while goalkeeper Mike Penders punched the ball into his own net to give Tottenham Hotspur a helping hand on their way to a second win at Stamford Bridge in 42 attempts.

This was hardly “the Battle of the Bridge”, but Chelsea blew up during a ridiculous 10-minute spell towards the end of a game in which Tottenham had bossed possession but not looked like scoring.

Palmer was lucky to stay on the pitch in the 70th minute, when he shoved his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes after the Tottenham midfielder had stopped him racing through with a foul and a handball.

Christopher Kavanagh, the referee, let him off with a yellow card, but 10 minutes later Palmer inexplicably gave Kavanagh no choice but to book him again and send him off, following a late challenge on substitute Conor Gallagher.

"It's PETULANT from Cole Palmer...you have to take it on the chin" Jamie Redknapp and Daniel Sturridge react to Cole Palmer's pair of yellow cards 🟥 https://t.co/Voxoo3Ea7V

Palmer was just about the only Chelsea player not to have been sent off last season, but it seems that Alonso has not yet managed to deal with the club’s disciplinary problem.

Jordan Henderson had given Palmer a talking to at the end of the win at Everton in which the forward was booked. But he evidently did not heed the advice or the words of his manager.

Alonso had said he was confident his players could keep calm ahead of the game, but he got that wrong – along with his team selection and substitutions.

In between Palmer’s two bookings, Penders suffered his own moment of madness with a bizarre own goal on his league debut for Chelsea. The Belgian was standing in for Emi Martinez, who watched in disbelief from the home dug-out after undergoing surgery on his jaw.

Fernandes sent in a corner that Jan Paul van Hecke challenged for. Penders looked like the easy winner in that contest, but he got his punch horribly wrong and the ball spun backwards and over the goalline.

Spurs have taken the lead after Mateus Fernandes' corner ends up in Chelsea's goal ⚽️ https://t.co/X65gyO9yPX

A man and a goal down, Chelsea then saw hundreds of their own fans walk out when Mathys Tel scored a brilliant second for Spurs with three minutes remaining. The visiting fans, who had seen one win at the Bridge since 1990 prior to Saturday, could hardly believe what they had seen.

"Just look what it means!" A glorious solo run and finish from Mathys Tel! 🤩 https://t.co/Qg7WMFNlwQ

Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi celebrated wildly with his staff. The two benches had clashed and De Zerbi had been booked after Palmer’s first yellow card that the Italian felt should have been a red. But De Zerbi will not care about that now, with Tottenham’s season finally up and running thanks to successive league wins against Coventry City and Chelsea.

"They were brilliant Spurs, they really were" Gary Neville's immediate reaction to Chelsea 0-2 Tottenham 🗣️ https://t.co/QWhi7Blmfz

Tottenham should really have been ahead in the first half. De Zerbi revealed before the game that Dominic Solanke had dropped down to the substitutes’ bench because the striker “felt fatigue” after the victory over Coventry.

With Solanke resting up on the bench until the 65th minute, De Zerbi moved Omar Marmoush, who had scored his first Spurs goal against Coventry, into the middle and brought in Tel on the left.

Tel was involved in the 29th-minute move that should have resulted in the opening goal for Marmoush. The Frenchman played a one-two with Andy Robertson and the Scotsman picked out Marmoush with a low cross. But, six yards out and with time to pick his spot, the former Manchester City man allowed Penders to make a save.

The missed Marmoush chance was the first time Penders had been called into action. At the other end, Tottenham goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky made unnecessary work for himself.

Kinsky played a bad pass straight to Pedro Neto. The ball was worked to Henderson, but Kinsky recovered to make a save and then stopped the follow-up from Neto. The offside flag then went up, but it was unclear whether it would have spared Kinsky on both occasions had Chelsea scored.

It was not the first time Kinsky had handed possession back to Chelsea in a dangerous area, although the 23-year-old had also made a good save to palm away a curling effort from Palmer. That came after Fernandes had the ball pinched from him far too easily.

Neto was Chelsea’s most dangerous player, but it was the wrong call by Alonso to leave Danny Welbeck on the bench, with João Pedro out injured, and he was too slow to change things. Leaving it until the 88th minute, when the game had already been killed by Tel, to send on the striker was a clear error.

Storm Boelo created wet-and-wild conditions on the Stamford Bridge pitch, while there were still remnants of Storm Austen, or should that be Storm Austin, on the home bench.

Chelsea set-piece coach Austin MacPhee let out an incredibly loud “for f---’s sake” when one corner routine went wrong. Nobody could hear what he was shouting over the Tottenham celebrations when Penders scored his own goal, but it would almost certainly have started with “f” again.

James Maddison had been a doubt before the game after missing training during the week and it only took four minutes of the second half for him to signal to De Zerbi that he needed to come off.

Maddison had scored a brilliant goal on his first league start in 18 months against Coventry, but he had to be replaced by former Chelsea midfielder Gallagher at Stamford Bridge.

James Maddison is forced off with an injury and is replaced by Conor Gallagher, who receives a mixed reception from his former fans 🔃 https://t.co/GSeXQQ3eoa

The Chelsea fans predictably booed Gallagher, a graduate of the club’s academy who at times even stood in as captain. The foul on Gallagher that earned Palmer his marching orders silenced the jeers and the Chelsea fans’ boos only returned at the final whistle for their own players.

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has told Cole Palmer he must learn from his red card that contributed to his team’s London derby defeat by Tottenham Hotspur.

Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi insisted Palmer should have seen red for shoving his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes. But, having got off with a yellow card, the Chelsea midfielder then fouled substitute Conor Gallagher.

“I haven’t seen them [the yellow cards] on TV, but as far as I have been told, he [the referee] probably got it right,” Alonso said. “So, for sure for Cole, but for everyone. We think [up until] now we haven’t received any red cards [this season] and we need to continue that way because we need to have this maturity to deal with difficult moments, when you have conceded 1-0, there was still 15-20 minutes to go, so we have to be calm. I need to check the action to talk with Cole, but it is one to learn for the future for sure.”

Asked if he thought Palmer should have been sent off for the first yellow card, De Zerbi, who was booked for his protests, replied: “Yep.”

Jordan Henderson had spoken to Palmer at the end of the previous week’s victory over Everton in which the forward could also have been booked for a second time and sent off.

But Alonso claimed he does not have any wider concerns about Palmer’s character. He said: “Today, for sure, yes, but it is not a [wider] concern. I think that Cole when he is focused on the game, when he is enjoying and today after the 1-0, it is a moment to keep calm, a moment to keep mature and for everyone.”

De Zerbi hailed his side’s character and claimed that Tottenham have “suffered enough” after two 17th-placed finishes and a slow start to the season until successive victories over Coventry City and Chelsea.

“We want to improve, improve and improve, to be better game by game, week by week. I think we have suffered enough,” De Zerbi said. “Changing the spirit of the group, changing the performance of the players, especially the more fragile players, maybe the younger players. We played very well. Great individual performances, great collective performance because we played very well. And then we put something different than Tottenham, I think, in the last period. Different attitude, different relationships with the players, different group.”

Chelsea were without João Pedro because of an injury and Alonso is waiting to find out how long the striker will be out.

“We don’t know yet because he has a lot of fluid,” Alonso said. “So he felt it yesterday [Friday] and we need to wait probably until tomorrow [Sunday] to do the test and to know the whole situation and the whole seriousness of the injury. We will know soon enough.”

A long-awaited Stamford Bridge victory for @SpursOfficial 👏 https://t.co/Qqwgbuj3Y3

“When we have dinner together and spend time together in the dressing room, I see a different group, different relationships and a different atmosphere among the players.

“The character was great today, but we have many, many new players. The players who stayed here from last season and two or three seasons ago suffered from the results, including two 17th-place finishes.

“We are working to change the last part of the club’s history. We are lucky because we have many great people in the dressing room and many great players. I think if we work hard, we can do something important.
